# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei ist Teil des Kuratierungsprozesses: Sie enthält die inhaltlichen
Leitplanken für alle KI-generierten Texte und Diagramme. Die maschinenlesbaren
Parameter dazu stehen in `ai/policy.json`; beide werden von
`ai_workflow.py auftrag` wörtlich in jeden Regenerierungsauftrag eingebettet.
Änderungen an Policy oder Richtlinien ⇒ `version` in `policy.json` erhöhen;
`ai_workflow.py status` zeigt dann, welche Fragmente noch mit einer älteren
Version erzeugt wurden.

## Geltungsbereich und Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch (`site.json → sprachen.kanonisch`). KI-Inhalte
  werden ausschließlich deutsch erzeugt; die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter
  Schritt (i18n_*.py) und niemals Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und `[SWS_…]`-Kennungen bleiben
  in jeder Sprache unverändert.

## Strukturelle Invarianten

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai` für
  Abschnitte, `ai usage` für Verwendungshinweise an Records, `ai module-guide`
  für Modul-Leitfäden) mit Badge und abschließender `<p class="ai-note">`
  (KI-Hinweis). Bestehende Fragmente sind die Referenz.
- Fragmente liegen unter `content/ai/<seiten-verzeichnis>/` und heißen
  `rec_<ELEMENT-ID>_<NN>.html` (an ein Spezifikationselement gebunden) oder
  `main_<NN>.html` (seitenbezogen).

## Belegpflicht und Quellen

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist mit `[SWS_…]`/`[RS_…]`-Zitat zu belegen
  (`policy.zitierpflicht`); Zitate verlinken auf das Quelldokument (PDF mit
  `#nameddest`), Richtwert `policy.relevanz.min_zitate_je_absatz`.
- Es dürfen nur Dokumente aus dem Quellenregister `ai/quellen.json` verwendet
  werden. Neue Quellen werden zuerst dort registriert (id, titel, typ, url).
- Aus Quellen extrahierte Einzelaussagen, auf die sich ein Text stützt, werden
  in der Trace unter `wissen[]` festgehalten: `{"aussage": …, "quelle": <id>,
  "fundstelle": …}`.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Spezifikation schweigt, darf die KI Lücken mit Annahmen schließen —
  höchstens `policy.annahmen.budget_je_text` pro Text bzw.
  `budget_je_diagramm` pro Diagramm.
- Jede Annahme wird (a) im Text als Interpretation erkennbar formuliert und
  (b) in der Trace unter `annahmen[]` protokolliert:
  `{"annahme": …, "begruendung": …}`.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekuliert.

## Diagramm-Entscheidung

Ein Diagramm wird nur eingefügt, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet
(`policy.diagramme`):

- Sequenzdiagramm (`.seq.json`): Abläufe mit ≥ `sequenz_ab_schritten`
  Schritten oder nicht offensichtlicher Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Strukturdiagramm (`.dot`): ≥ `kontext_ab_beteiligten` beteiligte
  Komponenten oder nicht-triviale Vererbungs-/Abhängigkeitscluster.
- Zustandsdiagramm (`.dot`): Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Die Entscheidung („warum dieses Diagramm, warum diese Form“), etwaige
Annahmen und das Denk-Transkript zur Quellenerstellung gehören in die Trace
unter `diagramme["<quellpfad>"]` — nicht ins HTML. Diagrammquellen liegen als
`<fragment-stem>.<diag-id>.dot|.seq.json` neben dem Fragment (inline) bzw.
unter `diagrams/` (seitenweite Diagramme); gerendert wird mit
`render_diagrams.py`. Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert.

        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Reads a complete line of characters into a String, advancing the current position accordingly. The end of the line is demarcated by the delimiter, or by \"\\\\n\" (ASCII 0x0a) if that parameter is omitted. The delimiter itself is not included in the returned String. Only Unicode code points with one character (code unit) can be used as delimiters. The returned string may start with an incomplete Unicode code point in case the current read position is in the middle of a code point. If the end of the file is reached, the remaining characters are returned and the current position is set to the end of the file. In case of an error, the current position is not changed.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"

        "tail": "\n"

      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Reads a number of characters into a String, starting from the current position. The returned string may start and/or end with incomplete Unicode code points in case the current read position and/or the last read character (code unit) is in the middle of a code point. The current position is advanced accordingly. If the end of the file is reached, the number of returned characters can be less than the requested number, and the current position is set to the end of the file. In case of an error, the current position is not changed.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"

        "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\"><a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>< void > WriteText (<a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_StringView_cfeb8f.html\">ara::core::StringView</a> s) noexcept;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Writes the content of a StringView to the file. The time when the content is persisted depends on the implementation of Persistency. SyncTo File can be used to force Persistency to persist the file content. In case of an error, the file content might be corrupted, and the current position might or might not have changed. The expected state of the file for each supported error can be expected to be as follows: • kPhysicalStorageFailure: The state of the file is unknown. It could have been entirely destroyed. • kEncryptionFailed: The content of the file and the current position will have been updated, but could not be persisted. The persisted file will reflect an older version of the file. • kOutOfStorageSpace: The content of the file will have been updated, but the part of the operation that exceeded the quota will have been discarded. The current position will be at the end of the file.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },

      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Resets a Key-Value Storage to the initial state. ResetKeyValueStorage allows to reset a Key-Value Storage to the initial state, containing only key-value pairs which were deployed from the Target Configuration, with their initial values. Afterwards, the Key-Value Storage will appear as if it was newly installed from the current Target Configuration. It will fail with kResourceBusy when the Key-Value Storage is currently open, or when it is modified by a call from another thread to UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, Reset Persistency, RecoverKeyValueStorage, or ResetKeyValueStorage.</p></div>",

      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Resets a file of this File Storage to its initial content. ResetFile allows to reset a single file to its initial content. If the file is currently not available in the File Storage, it is re-created. Afterwards, the file will appear in both cases as if it was newly installed from the current Target Configuration.         "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\"><a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>< void > WriteBinary (<a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Span_f16d72.html\">ara::core::Span</a>< const <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"../namespaces/ns_core_ara_core_e30e31.html#SWS_CORE_04200\">ara::core::Byte</a> > b) noexcept;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Writes the content of a Span of Byte to the file. The time when the content is persisted depends on the implementation of Persistency. SyncTo File can be used to force Persistency to persist the file content. In case of an error, the file content might be corrupted, and the current position might or might not have changed. The expected state of the file for each supported error can be expected to be as follows: • kPhysicalStorageFailure: The state of the file is unknown. It could have been entirely destroyed. • kEncryptionFailed: The content of the file and the current position will have been updated, but could not be persisted. The persisted file will reflect an older version of the file. • kOutOfStorageSpace: The content of the file will have been updated, but the part of the operation that exceeded the quota will have been discarded. The current position will be at the end of the file.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },

        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\"><a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>< void > ResetKey (<a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_StringView_cfeb8f.html\">ara::core::StringView</a> key) noexcept;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"

      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Resets a key of this Key-Value Storage to its initial value. ResetKey allows to reset a single key to its initial value. If the key is currently not available in the Key-Value Storage, it is re-created. Afterwards, the key-value pair will appear in both cases as if it was newly installed from the current Target Configuration. ResetKey will fail with kInitValueNotAvailable when neither Application Design nor Target Configuration define an initial value for the key. ResetKey may be delayed by an ongoing call from another thread to RemoveAllKeys, SyncTo Storage, or DiscardPendingChanges, or to SetValue, GetValue, GetCurrentValueSize, Remove Key, RecoverKey, or ResetKey for the same key-value pair.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"

      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Recovers a single key-value pair of this Key Value Storage. This method allows to recover a single key-value pair when the redundancy checks fail. This method does a best-effort recovery of the key-value pair. After recovery, the key-value pair might contain outdated or initial content, or might be lost. RecoverKey may be delayed by an ongoing call from another thread to RemoveAllKeys, SyncTo Storage, or DiscardPendingChanges, or to SetValue, GetValue, GetCurrentValueSize, Remove Key, RecoverKey, or ResetKey for the same key-value pair.</p></div>",

      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Opens a file of this File Storage for reading and writing with a user provided buffer. If not otherwise specified by the provided mode, the file is opened with the seek position set to the beginning (corresponding to kAtTheBeginning). The provided buffer will be used by the ReadWriteAccessor to implement block-wise reading and writing to speed up multiple small accesses to the file. If the file does not exist, it is created. The file will be closed when the returned UniqueHandle goes out of scope.</p></div>",

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n1 Introduction and Functional Overview\nThis document is the software specification of the\nPersistency functional\ncluster\nwithin the\nAdaptive Platform\n. The\nPersistency functional clus-\nter\nwill be referenced as\nPersistency\nin the remainder of this document.\nPersistency\noffers mechanisms to\nAdaptive Applications\nand other\nfunc-\ntional clusters\nto store information in the non-volatile memory of a machine. The\ndata is available over boot and ignition cycles.\nThe\nPersistency\nwill typically be implemented as a library that runs within a\nPro-\ncess\nof an\nAdaptive Application\n, with the rights of that\nProcess\n.\n10 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P11_15",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 11,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n2 Acronyms and Abbreviations\nThe glossary below includes acronyms and abbreviations relevant to the\nPersis-\ntency\nthat are not included in the [1, AUTOSAR glossary]."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P11_16",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 11,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "This version identifies the structural layout of\nPersistency\n.\nThe\ncontract version\nis expected to change when\nStor-\nages\nare added, removed, or renamed, when their access mode\nchanges, or when the available data types of a\nKey-Value\nStorage\nor the data types of\nstorage elements\nchange."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P11_17",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 11,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "This version identifies the pre-installed content of\nPersistency\n.\nThe\ndeployment version\nis expected to change when pre-\ninstalled\nelements\nof otherwise unchanged\nstorages\nare\nadded, removed, or renamed."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P11_18",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 11,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Persistency\ndistinguishes data integrity, which is ensured by\nthe configured\nredundancy\n, from structural integrity, i.e. the\nreadability of the structure of a\nKey-Value Storage\nor\nFile\nStorage\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P11_19",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 11,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "11 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P12_20",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 12,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P12_21",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 12,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Persistency\nsupports different mechanisms to access data in\npersistent memory. Concurrent access to the data by several\nProcess\nes is not supported as the data is owned exclusively by\none\nProcess\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P12_22",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 12,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "The actual physical memory on which\npersistent data\nis\nstored. This could be a flash device that is accessed directly\nby\nPersistency\n, or a file system of the OS that uses an SSD."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P12_23",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 12,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Redundancy is used by\nPersistency\nto ensure the\nin-\ntegrity\nof stored data. It can be configured to use replication\nof stored data, CRCs, or Hashes. Typically, only replication will\nallow to repair corrupted data."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P12_24",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 12,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Persistency\nuses update strategies configured on\nelement\nand\nstorage\nlevel. The actual\nupdate strategy\nof an\nel-\nement\nis derived from\nmanifest\nparameters for the\nelement\nand the containing\nstorage\ndefined during design and deploy-\nment phase."
    },

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n3 Related Documentation\n3.1 Input Documents & Related Standards and Norms\n[1] Glossary\nAUTOSAR_FO_TR_Glossary\n[2] Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core\n[3] Specification of Manifest\nAUTOSAR_AP_TPS_ManifestSpecification\n[4] Explanation of Adaptive Platform Software Architecture\nAUTOSAR_AP_EXP_SWArchitecture\n[5] Requirements on Persistency\nAUTOSAR_AP_RS_Persistency\n[6] General Requirements specific to Adaptive Platform\nAUTOSAR_AP_RS_General\n[7] Specification of Update and Configuration Management\nAUTOSAR_AP_SWS_UpdateAndConfigurationManagement\n[8] Explanation of Adaptive Platform Design\nAUTOSAR_AP_EXP_PlatformDesign\n[9] Specification of Cryptography\nAUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Cryptography\n[10] Specification of Platform Types for Adaptive Platform\nAUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformTypes\n[11] Specification of Language Binding for modeled AP data types\nAUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LanguageBindingForModeledAPdatatypes\n3.2 Further Applicable Specifications\nAUTOSAR provides a core specification [2] which is also applicable for the\nPersis-\ntency\n. The chapter General requirements for all FunctionalClusters of this specifica-\ntion shall be considered as an additional and required specification for implementation\nof the\nPersistency\n.\n13 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P14_27",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 14,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4 Constraints and Assumptions\n4.1 Known Limitations\n\u000f\nAlthough a\nKey-Value Storage\nand\nFile Storage\ncan be configured as\nwrite-only, the current API always allows read access. Read access is even pos-\nsible when a\nfile\nhas been opened with\nara::per::FileStorage::Open-\nFileWriteOnly\n.\n4.2 Constraints on Configuration\nThere are several constraints on the\nPersistency\nconfiguration that need to be ob-\nserved by the tooling which creates/processes this part of the\nExecution Manifest\n.\nThese constraints are defined in [3].\n4.3 Assumptions about the Implementation of Persistency\nPersistency\ncan be implemented with different internal architectures, and at the\nsame time,\napplications\nand other\nfunctional clusters\nexpect a well defined\nbehavior that is independent of the actual implementation of\nPersistency\n. There-\nfore, the specification in this document needs to be sufficiently generic to cover the\nunderlying differences. As usual in AUTOSAR Adaptive, the actual implementation is\nnot defined by the specification and is therefore entirely up to the vendor of\nPersis-\ntency\n.\nThe following subsections list some of the possible implementations of\nPersistency\n.\n4.3.1 Library Only\nIn this scenario,\nPersistency\nconsists solely of a library. The manifest is partly used\nto configure the compilation of the library (design time parts) and partly transferred to\na configuration file that is read by\nPersistency\nat run-time (deployment parts).\nThere is still some freedom regarding the storage of\nmetadata\nand actual data, and\nregarding the points in time when\nelements\nof a\nstorage\nare checked regarding re-\ndundancy or authenticity or when they are decrypted. E.g. the whole\nFile Storage\ncould be checked when it is opened or the single\nfiles\ncould be checked when they\nare opened.\n14 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P15_28",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 15,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4.3.2 Using a Central Daemon\nIn this scenario, the\nPersistency\nlibrary connects in the background to a daemon\nvia some IPC mechanism. The manifest influences again the compilation of the library\npart and is also transferred to configuration files for the library part and possibly also\nthe daemon.\nAn implementer has the same freedom regarding data storage, encryption, and checks\nfor redundancy and authenticity as in the last scenario. But an additional challenge is\nthat the communication channel between library and daemon can be lost at any time,\nresulting in additional potential errors.\n4.3.3 Based on a File System\nBoth a library and a daemon can access\nstorage\nusing the file system services of\nthe operating system. In this case, because AUTOSAR Adaptive is based on POSIX,\nthe file systems will be mounted with specific options that are out of control of the\nPersistency\nimplementation, but influence the point in time when written data ac-\ntually appears on the disc. Due to this, it is not possible to guarantee synchronous\nbehavior for calls like\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SyncToStorage\nor\nara::\nper::ReadWriteAccessor::SyncToFile\n.\n4.3.4 Direct Access to Storage Hardware\nIndependently of whether a daemon is used or not,\nPersistency\ncan be implemented\nto access hardware devices like flash memory directly. These devices have the intrinsic\nproblem that the signal that can be read from each memory cell is reduced over time,\nmainly influenced by the number of write accesses. In the end, the cell will produce\narbitrary values on each read access.\nUnfortunately, the distribution of write accesses in typical systems is very uneven.\nSome parameters might be updated a few times a second, while some code may stay\nuntouched for the whole life time of the ECU. To avoid early read errors, wear leveling\nshould be deployed, such that frequent updates of single data elements are distributed\nover the whole memory area.\nOn the other hand, most operating systems include a file system or at least a flash\ndriver that takes care of wear leveling, such that a typical implementation of the\nPer-\nsistency\nwill not have to care about the wear leveling. This use case is therefore not\ndescribed in any detail in this specification.\n15 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },

      "source_page": 16,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n5 Dependencies to Other Functional Clusters\nThis chapter provides an overview of the dependencies to other\nFunctional Clus-\nters\nin the AUTOSAR\nAdaptive Platform\n.     {

    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P32_108",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 32,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7 Functional Specification\n7.1 The Architecture of Persistency\nThe\nPersistency\noffers two different mechanisms to access persistent memory:\nKey-Value Storages\noffer access to a set of\nkeys\nwith associated\nvalues\n(similar\nto a database), while\nFile Storages\noffer access to a set of\nfiles\n(similar to a\ndirectory of a file system).\nThe typical usage of the\nPersistency\nwithin an\nAdaptive Application\nis de-\npicted in Figure 7.1. As shown there, an\nAdaptive Application\ncan use a combi-\nnation of multiple\nKey-Value Storages\nand multiple\nFile Storages\n. Of course,\nthe same applies to other\nfunctional clusters\nusing\nPersistency\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P32_109",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 32,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.1: Typical usage of\nPersistency\nwithin an\nAdaptive Application\nPersistency\ncan also be used directly by other\nFunctional Clusters\nwithout\ninvolvement of the\napplication\n. The library part of these\nFunctional Clusters\nwill use dedicated deployment information of\nPersistency\n, while Daemons of\nFunc-\ntional Clusters\ncan be modeled similarly to\nAdaptive Applications\n.\n7.1.1 Persistency in the Manifest\nThe\nPersistency\nusage of an\nAdaptive Application\nis modeled in the\nExe-\ncution Manifest\n(furtheron simply referred to as the \nmanifest\n) as part of the\n32 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P33_110",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 33,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nAdaptiveApplicationSwComponentType\ns of an\nExecutable\n. The model has\ntwo principal parts: The application design information, aggregated by the\nPersis-\ntencyKeyValueStorageInterface\nand the\nPersistencyFileStorageInter-\nface\n, and the deployment information, aggregated by the\nPersistencyKeyVal-\nueStorage\nand the\nPersistencyFileStorage\n. The latter is also used when the\nPersistency\nis accessed directly by another\nFunctional Cluster\n.\nThe API specification holds the classes\nara::per::KeyValueStorage\nand\nara::\nper::FileStorage\nfor access to a\nKey-Value Storage\nor a\nFile Storage\n, re-\nspectively. The global functions of these classes receive either the identifier (the fully\nqualified\nshortName\npath) of a\nPortPrototype\ntyped by a\nPersistencyInter-\nface\n, or the\nshortName\npath of a\nFunctionalClusterInteractsWithPersis-\ntencyDeploymentMapping\n. Both are then used as an\nara::core::Instance-\nSpecifier\ninput parameter (see subsection 8.2.1 and subsection 8.3.1). Depend-\ning on the nature of the\nPortPrototype\nor on the value of\nFunctionalCluster-\nInteractsWithPersistencyDeploymentMapping\n.\npersistencyAccess\n, the\nKey-Value Storage\nor\nFile Storage\nwill be accessible as:\nRead Only\nif the\nPortPrototype\nis instantiated as\nRPortPrototype\nor\nFunc-\ntionalClusterInteractsWithPersistencyDeploymentMapping\n.\npersistencyAccess\nis\nread\n, or\nRead/Write\nif the\nPortPrototype\nis instantiated as\nPRPortPrototype\nor\nFunctionalClusterInteractsWithPersistencyDeploymentMapping\n.\npersistencyAccess\nis\nreadWrite\n, or\nWrite Only\nif the\nPortPrototype\nis instantiated as\nPPortPrototype\nor\nFunc-\ntionalClusterInteractsWithPersistencyDeploymentMapping\n.\npersistencyAccess\nis\nwrite\n.\nIn case of application access to Persistency, the\nmanifest\ncontains separate de-\nployment data for each\nProcess\nthat references the\nExecutable\n. The\nProcess\nis bound to the deployment data by specialization of the class\nPersistencyPort-\nPrototypeToDeploymentMapping\n, which refers to a\nPortPrototype\ntyped by a\nPersistencyInterface\n, a\nPersistencyDeployment\n, and the\nProcess\n."

      "verbatim_text": "And the link between application design and deployment information, represented by\nPersistencyPortPrototypeToDeploymentMapping\n, is specialized as\nPersis-\ntencyPortPrototypeToKeyValueStorageMapping\nand\nPersistencyPort-\nPrototypeToFileStorageMapping\n.\n7.1.2 Key-Value Storages in the Manifest\nEvery\nKey-Value Storage\nis either represented by a\nPortPrototype\ntyped by\na\nPersistencyKeyValueStorageInterface\nin the application design for the re-\nspective\nAdaptiveApplicationSwComponentType\n, or by a\nFunctionalClus-\nterInteractsWithPersistencyDeploymentMapping\n, and in both cases by a\nPersistencyKeyValueStorage\ncontaining deployment information.       "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P36_115",

      "source_page": 36,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2 General Features of Persistency\n[SWS_PER_00002]\nd\nAll specified classes within the\nPersistency\nshall reside within\nthe C++ namespace\nara::per\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00115)\n7.2.1 Functional Cluster Lifecycle\n7.2.1.1 Initialization and Shutdown of Persistency\nUsing\nara::core::Initialize\nand\nara::core::Deinitialize\n, the applica-\ntion initializes and de-initializes all\nfunctional clusters\nwith direct ARA interfaces\n(i.e. the\nAdaptive Platform Foundation\n).\n[SWS_PER_00408]\nd\nWhen\nara::core::Initialize\nis called, the\nPersistency\nshall read in the\nmanifest\ninformation and prepare the access structures to all\nKey-\n-Value Storages\nand\nFile Storages\nthat are defined in the\nmanifest\n.\nc\n(RS_-\nPER_00018)\n[SWS_PER_00409]\nd\nWhen\nara::core::Deinitialize\nis called, the\nPersis-\ntency\nshall implicitly ensure that all open\nfiles\nof all\nFile Storages\nare per-\nsisted as though\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::SyncToFile\nwas called and\nclosed as though the\nara::per::UniqueHandle\ns were destructed, and that not\npersisted\nvalues\nin all\nKey-Value Storages\nare dropped as though\nara::per::\nKeyValueStorage::DiscardPendingChanges\nwas called. Afterwards,\nPersis-\ntency\nshall free remaining resources that are not exposed by objects held by the ap-\nplication, including but not limited to the configuration of\nPersistency\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_-\n00018)\nThe\napplication\nis expected not to call any API of\nPersistency\n(directly or in-\ndirectly through other\nfunctional clusters\n) before calling\nara::core::Ini-\ntialize\nor after calling\nara::core::Deinitialize\n, but\nPersistency\nneeds to\nprotect itself against such eventualities.\n[SWS_PER_00410]\n{DRAFT}\nd\nAll functions of\nPersistency\nand all methods of its\nclasses shall call\nara::core::Abort\nwhen they are called after static initializa-\ntion but before\nara::core::Initialize\nwas called or after\nara::core::Deini-\ntialize\nwas called.\nc\n(RS_PER_00018)\n36 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2.2 Error Handling\nError handling in\nPersistency\nis aligned with the guidelines described in [2]. To this\nend, the\nPersistency\nhas to implement a set of standard classes and APIs, which\nare described in this section.\n[SWS_PER_00472]\nd\nPersistency\nshall use the error codes defined in\nara::per::\nPerErrc\nto report problems to the calling\napplication\nvia\nara::core::Result\n.\nVendors of\nPersistency\nmay add their own errors to\nara::per::PerErrc\n, using\ncodes above\n255\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nara::per::PerErrc\nbelongs to the\nara::per::PerErrorDomain\n, which can be\nused by an\napplication\nto classify returned errors.\n[SWS_PER_00473]\nd\nara::per::GetPerDomain\nshall return the global\nara::\nper::PerErrorDomain\nobject.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nTo create its own\nPersistency\nerror codes, the\napplication\nmay use\nara::\nper::MakeErrorCode\n.\n[SWS_PER_00474]\nd\nara::per::MakeErrorCode\nshall return an\nara::core::\nErrorCode\nwhen called with an error code from\nara::per::PerErrc\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_-\n00128)\n[SWS_PER_00353]\nd\nara::per::PerErrorDomain::Name\nshall return the NUL-\nterminated string Per.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\n[SWS_PER_00475]\nd\nara::per::PerErrorDomain::Message\nshall return the er-\nror message associated with the passed\nara::core::ErrorCode\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nThe whole\nPersistency\nAPI has been designed to be exception-less. If an\nap-\nplication\nprefers to use exceptions, it may use\nara::per::PerErrorDomain::\nThrowAsException\n, or simply\nara::core::ErrorCode::ThrowAsException\n.\n[SWS_PER_00476]\nd\nara::per::PerErrorDomain::ThrowAsException\nshall\nthrow an\nara::per::PerException\nthat is created from the passed error code.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\n[SWS_PER_00571]\nd\nWhen\nPersistency\ndetects an inconsistency in the\nmanifest\nincluding invalid or non-existing URIs, it shall treat this situation as a violation as defined\nin [2] and call\nara::core::Abort\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00149)\n7.2.2.1 Handling of General Errors\n[SWS_PER_00536]\nd\nWhen a function or method of\nPersistency\nencounters a prob-\nlem with the hardware or the underlaying operating system services during the access\nto a\nstorage\nor an\nelement\nof a\nstorage\n,\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkPhysicalStorageFailure\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\n37 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P38_117",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00537",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 38,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nWhen\nkPhysicalStorageFailure\noccurs, the\napplication\ncannot access the\naffected\nstorage\nany more. Depending on the system, a reboot might restore the\naccess.\n[SWS_PER_00537]\nd\nWhen a method of\nPersistency\nwould modify the underlying\nstorage\n, but the\nstorage\nis configured as read-only (the\nPortPrototype\nthat is\ntyped by the corresponding\nPersistencyInterface\nis instantiated as\nRPortPro-\ntotype\n),\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkIllegalWriteAccess\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_-\n00128)\n[SWS_PER_00538]\nd\nWhen a function of\nPersistency\nis called with an\nara::\ncore::InstanceSpecifier\nthat is not available in the\nmanifest\n,\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkStorageNotFound\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nThe two previous errors (\nkIllegalWriteAccess\nand\nkStorageNotFound\n) occur\nwhen the configuration does not match the implemented access to a\nstorage\n. An\napplication\nmight be implemented to be aware of this possibility and react accord-\ningly to the error by avoiding (write) accesses to the\nstorage\n. If the\napplication\ndepends on (write) access to the\nstorage\n, these errors would hint at an incorrect\nconfiguration of the\nstorage\n.\n[SWS_PER_00539]\nd\nWhen a function or method of\nPersistency\ndetects a funda-\nmental problem in the structure of the\nstorage\nthat prevents accessing the\nstorage\n,\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkIntegrityCorrupted\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nThe\napplication\ncan restore a corrupted\nstorage\nby calling\nara::per::Recov-\nerKeyValueStorage\n,\nara::per::ResetKeyValueStorage\n,\nara::per::Re-\ncoverAllFiles\n, or\nara::per::ResetAllFiles\n. When the\nkIntegrityCor-\nrupted\nis reported for an\nelement\nof a\nstorage\n,\nintegrity\ncan be restored\nby calling\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::RecoverKey\n,\nara::per::KeyVal-\nueStorage::ResetKey\n,\nara::per::FileStorage::RecoverFile\n, or\nara::\nper::FileStorage::ResetFile\n.\nWhen\nPersistency\ndetects insufficient or broken redundancy, it will report\nkVali-\ndationFailed\nas described in [SWS_PER_00221].\n[SWS_PER_00540]\nd\nWhen encryption or decryption of\npersistent data\nfails\nwithin a function or method of\nPersistency\n,\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkEncryptionFailed\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\n[SWS_PER_00564]\nd\nWhen the calculation or verification of the\nMAC\nof\npersistent\ndata\nfails within a function or method of\nPersistency\n,\nPersistency\nshall return\nthe error\nkAuthenticationFailed\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nThe two previous errors can occur when the configured cryptographic keys or algo-\nrithms are not available at run time, or when the\nstorage\nor the\nelement\nof a\nstor-\nage\nis corrupted. The latter case could be detected or even avoided by configuring\nredundancy\n.\n38 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P39_118",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00541",

      "source_page": 39,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_PER_00541]\nd\nWhen a method of\nPersistency\ntries to read data from a\nfile\n,\nbut the position is already at the end,\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkIsEof\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nThis error can typically be dealt with by the\napplication\n, and can be avoided by\nusing\nara::per::ReadAccessor::IsEof\n.\n[SWS_PER_00542]\nd\nWhen a function or method of\nPersistency\nwould create a\nfile\n, but the number of existing\nfiles\nalready equals the configured\nPersistency-\nFileStorageInterface\n.\nmaxNumberOfFiles\nof the corresponding\nFile Stor-\nage\n,\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkTooManyFiles\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nThis error might occur when a new\nfile\nis opened for writing, or when a\nFile Stor-\nage\nis updated or when it is recovered after an error. An\napplication\nseeing this\nerror might delete some\nfiles\nto be able to create the new\nfile\n(or\nfiles\n), or reset\nthe\nFile Storage\nto the initial state using\nara::per::ResetAllFiles\nor\nara::\nper::ResetPersistency\n.\n[SWS_PER_00543]\nd\nWhen a function or method of\nPersistency\nwould increase the\nsize of a\nstorage\nor an\nelement\nof a\nstorage\nsuch that the total storage size would\nexceed the configured\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nmaximumAllowedSize\nof the\nstorage\n,\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkQuotaExceeded\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nThis error means that the\napplication\ntried to store data that exceeds the\nconfigured quota of a\nstorage\n. The\napplication\nhas to be able to deal\nwith this situation, and either write less data to the affected\nstorage\nor re-\nmove outdated data from this\nstorage\n, or reset the affected\nelement\n/\nstor-\nage\nwith a call to\nara::per::ResetKeyValueStorage\n,\nara::per::ResetAll-\nFiles\n,\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::ResetKey\n,\nara::per::FileStor-\nage::ResetFile\n, or even\nara::per::ResetPersistency\n.\n[SWS_PER_00544]\nd\nWhen a function or method of\nPersistency\ncannot increase\nthe size of a\nstorage\nbecause the\nphysical storage\nis not sufficient (e.g. file\nsystem quoata exceeded or partition full),\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkOut-\nOfStorageSpace\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nThis error means that some other\nstorage\nor even a completely independent process\noccupies so much\nphysical storage\nthat\nPersistency\ncannot store additional\ndata. This can only happen if\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nmaximumAllowedSize\nis\nconfigured to a higher value than\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nminimumSustained-\nSize\n. The\napplication\nhas to be able to deal with this situation, and either write less\ndata to the affected\nstorage\nor remove outdated data from this or another\nstorage\n,\nor reset this or another\nelement\n/\nstorage\nwith a call to\nara::per::ResetKeyVal-\nueStorage\n,\nara::per::ResetAllFiles\n,\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::\nResetKey\n,\nara::per::FileStorage::ResetFile\n, or even\nara::per::Re-\nsetPersistency\n.\n39 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },

      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P40_119",

      "source_page": 40,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2.3 Parallel Access to Persistent Data\nAccording to [8], the\npersistent data\nis local to one\nProcess\n. Therefore,\nPer-\nsistency\nwill never share\npersistent data\nbetween two (or more)\nProcess\nes,\neven of the same\nExecutable\n. The background of this decision is that\nPersistency\nshould not provide an additional communication path for\napplications\nbesides the\nmechanisms provided by the\nfunctional cluster\nCommunication Management\n(e.g. using ara::com).\n[SWS_PER_00309]\nd\nPersistent data\nshall always be local to one\nProcess\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00001)\nIf\npersistent data\nneeds to be accessed by multiple\nProcess\nes (of the same or\ndifferent\napplications\n), it is the duty of the application designer to provide\nService\nInterfaces\nfor communication.\nPersistency\nis, on the other hand, prepared to handle concurrent access from mul-\ntiple threads of the same\napplication\n, running in the context of the same\nProcess\n.\nTo create shared access to a\nKey-Value Storage\nor\nFile Storage\n, either the\nara::per::SharedHandle\nreturned by\nara::per::OpenKeyValueStorage\nand\nara::per::OpenFileStorage\ncan be passed on (i.e. copied) to another thread, or\nara::per::OpenKeyValueStorage\nand\nara::per::OpenFileStorage\ncan be\ncalled in independent threads for the same\nKey-Value Storage\nor\nFile Storage\n,\nrespectively. All operations of the\nKey-Value Storage\nand\nFile Storage\nsupport\nconcurrent access from multiple threads, though operations like\nara::per::Recov-\nerKeyValueStorage\nand\nara::per::ResetKeyValueStorage\nor\nara::per::\nRecoverAllFiles\nand\nara::per::ResetAllFiles\nwill only succeed when the\ncorresponding\nKey-Value Storage\nor\nFile Storage\nis not opened.\n[SWS_PER_00545]\nd\nWhen a function of\nPersistency\nthat modifies a\nstorage\nis\ncalled while another function that modifies the same\nstorage\nis being executed,\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkResourceBusy\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nThis restriction also applies to global functions like\nara::per::UpdatePersis-\ntency\n, which will only succeed if no\nstorage\nis open, and no other thread is currently\nmodifying a\nstorage\nwith functions like\nara::per::RecoverKeyValueStorage\nor\nara::per::ResetAllFiles\n.\nAccess to single\nkey-value pairs\nof a\nKey-Value Storage\nis possi-\nble from multiple threads at the same time, because the operation of\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetValue\nand\nara::per::KeyValueStor-\nage::SetValue\nare atomic, as are those of\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::Re-\nmoveKey\n,\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::RemoveAllKeys\n,\nara::per::Key-\nValueStorage::SyncToStorage\n, and\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::Dis-\ncardPendingChanges\n.\nAccess to single\nfiles\nof a\nFile Storage\ncannot be shared between multiple\nthreads, because it would be impossible to synchronize read and write accesses and\nthe corresponding change of the seek position in a\nfile\n. Accordingly, the\nara::\n40 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nper::UniqueHandle\nreturned by the\nOpenFile\n*\nAPIs can only be moved to an-\nother thread, and trying to open an already opened\nfile\nwill fail. Likewise, operations\nlike\nara::per::FileStorage::DeleteFile\n,\nara::per::FileStorage::Re-\ncoverFile\n, and\nara::per::FileStorage::ResetFile\nwill also not be possible\non open\nfiles\n.\n[SWS_PER_00546]\nd\nWhen a method of\nara::per::FileStorage\nthat opens or\nmodifies a\nfile\nis called while the same\nfile\nis currently open or being modified\nby another method,\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkResourceBusy\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_-\n00128)\nFiles\nare implicitly closed when their\nara::per::UniqueHandle\ngoes out of\nscope, or when the\nFile Storage\nto which they belong is closed.\n[SWS_PER_00425]\nd\nWhen a\nFile Storage\nis closed, because all related\nara::\nper::SharedHandle\ns go out of scope, any\nfiles\nwhich are still open are also\nclosed.\nc\n(RS_PER_00001)\nAccessing a\nara::per::UniqueHandle\nof a\nfile\nof a closed\nFile Storage\nwill\nresult in undefined behavior.\n41 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P42_121",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00210",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 42,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2.4 Security Concepts\nThe\nPersistency\nsupports protection of the authenticity and confidentiality of data\nstored in a\nKey-Value Storage\nor\nFile Storage\n. Which kind of protection is\napplied and the used algorithms are decided at deployment time. The\napplication\nis not aware of this fact.\nIf confidentiality of data shall be protected, a\nstorage\nor an\nelement\nof a\nstorage\nare encrypted after the creation of the\nstorage\nand when the\nstorage\nis saved, and\nare decrypted when a\nstorage\nis opened. Therefore, only encrypted data is stored\npersistently. In case of a read-only\nstorage\n, encryption is done only once during\ninstallation, decryption is done every time the\nstorage\nis opened.\nIf authenticity of data shall be protected, a message authentication code (\nMAC\n) is gen-\nerated after the creation of a\nstorage\nand when the\nstorage\nis saved, and verified\nwhen the\nstorage\nis opened. Therefore, unauthorized modifications to the\nstorage\ncan be detected.\nIn case of a read-only\nstorage\n, it is also possible to protect the authenticity of the\nstorage\n(or an\nelement\ntherein) by calculating a hash value of the data to be pro-\ntected and comparing this calculated value to a hash value provided in the\nmanifest\n.\nThis assumes that the authenticity of the processed       "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2.5 Redundancy Concepts\nThe\nPersistency\nshall take care of the integrity of the stored data, both for safety\npurposes and to prevent data loss. This can be achieved by calculating CRCs or hash\nvalues of the stored data, and by creating redundant copies. All these measures ef-\nfectively create some\nredundancy\nfor the stored data. The concrete measures to be\ntaken are configurable: The application designer can use\nPersistencyInterface\n.\nredundancy\nto request\nredundancy\n(by setting it to\nredundant\nor\nredundant-\nPerElement\n), or use\nPersistencyInterface\n.\nredundancyHandling\nto prese-\nlect the actual measures to be taken. During deployment, the integrator can define the\nactual measures taken to ensure data integrity using\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nre-\ndundancyHandling\n. If\nPersistencyInterface\n.\nredundancyHandling\nis con-\nfigured, the integrator shall use it as a guidance, but may also choose other, more\nappropriate measures based on superior knowledge of the final system.\n[SWS_PER_00317]\nd\nThe\nPersistency\nshall store redundant information for ev-\nery\nstorage\nrepresented by a\nPersistencyDeployment\nwhere\nPersisten-\ncyDeployment\n.\nredundancyHandling\nis configured.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008, RS_PER_-\n00009, RS_PER_00010)\nThe actual handling of the\nredundancy\nconfigured during deployment is described\nin the following sections, see also [SWS_PER_00318], [SWS_PER_00319], and\n[SWS_PER_00447].\n[SWS_PER_00221]\nd\nPersistency\nshall check the redundant data when accessing\nstored data. When the stored data is corrupted,\nPersistency\nshall try to restore it\nusing the available\nredundancy\n. If\nPersistency\nis not able to recover using the\nredundancy\n, it shall report\nkValidationFailed\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008)\nDepending on the actual implementation,\nPersistency\nmight access the stored data\nat different times, e.g. when\nara::core::Initialize\nis called, when a\nKey-\n-Value Storage\nis opened, or when a\nfile\nis accessed. The question whether\nthe\nredundancy\nis sufficient for recovery is also implementation specific and can only\nbe safely assumed for\nPersistencyRedundancyMOutOfN\n.\nWhen the recovery failed, the\napplication\ncan choose to use\nara::per::Recov-\nerKeyValueStorage\n,\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::RecoverKey\n,\nara::\nper::RecoverAllFiles\n, or\nara::per::FileStorage::RecoverFile\nto re-\ncover as much as possible and set the corresponding\nKey-Value Storage\nor\nFile\nStorage\nagain into a consistent state.\n[SWS_PER_00452]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::RecoverKeyValueStorage\nis called,\nPersistency\nshall restore the\nKey-Value Storage\nto a consistent state, including\nredundancy\n. First, the infrastructure of the whole\nKey-Value Storage\nshall be re-\nstored, then\nPersistency\nshall try to recover all\nkey-value pairs\navailable in the\nKey-Value Storage\nas described in [SWS_PER_00453]. Depending on available\ninformation, the whole\nKey-Value Storage\nmight be reset to the initial state as de-\nscribed in [SWS_PER_00456], losing all updated\nvalues\nof its\nkey-value pairs\n,\nor may contain outdated\nkey-value pairs\nafter the operation.\nc\n(RS_PER_00009)\n45 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_PER_00547]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::RecoverKey\nis\ncalled,\nPersistency\nshall first check whether the\nkey-value pair\nis present\nin any instance of the\nKey-Value Storage\n, and otherwise return directly with\nkKeyNotFound\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\n[SWS_PER_00453]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::RecoverKey\nis\ncalled for an existing\nkey-value pair\n,\nPersistency\nshall try to restore the\ngiven\nkey\nto a consistent state, including\nredundancy\n. Depending on available\ninformation, the\nkey\nmight be removed, reset to the initial\nvalue\nas described\nin [SWS_PER_00477], or might contain an outdated\nvalue\nafter the operation.\nc\n(RS_PER_00009)\n[SWS_PER_00454]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::RecoverAllFiles\nis called,\nPersis-\ntency\nshall restore the\nFile Storage\nto a consistent state, including\nredundancy\n.\nFirst, the infrastructure of the whole\nFile Storage\nshall be restored as described\nin [SWS_PER_00478], then\nPersistency\nshall try to recover all currently available\nfiles\nas described in [SWS_PER_00455]. Depending on available information, the\nwhole\nFile Storage\nmight be reset to the initial state, losing all updated content of\nits\nfiles\n, or may contain outdated\nfiles\nafter the operation.\nc\n(RS_PER_00009)\n[SWS_PER_00548]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::RecoverFile\nis called,\nPersistency\nshall first check whether the\nfile\nis present in the\nFile Storage\n,\nand otherwise return directly with\nkFileNotFound\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\n[SWS_PER_00455]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::RecoverFile\nis called for\nan existing\nfile\n,\nPersistency\nshall try to restore the given\nfile\nto a consistent\nstate, including\nredundancy\n. Depending on available information, the\nfile\nmight be\nremoved, reset to the initial state as described in [SWS_PER_00479], or might contain\noutdated content after the operation.\nc\n(RS_PER_00009)\nOf course the\napplication\nhas to validate the restored data in this case.\nOr it can use\nara::per::ResetPersistency\n(see [SWS_PER_00556]),\nara::per::ResetKeyValueStorage\n(see [SWS_PER_00456]),\nara::per::\nKeyValueStorage::ResetKey\n(see [SWS_PER_00477]),\nara::per::Rese-\ntAllFiles\n(see [SWS_PER_00478]), or\nara::per::FileStorage::ResetFile\n(see [SWS_PER_00479]) to reset the corrupted item to the initial state according to\nthe current\nmanifest\n.\nThe\napplication\nmay want to monitor its\nstorages\nfor any problem detected by\nredundancy\n, even if\nPersistency\nis able to recover by itself. This might be required\nto e.g. get an early indication of hardware problems or for safety critical\napplica-\ntions\n. This monitoring is supported by\nPersistency\n, which will trigger a callback\nfunction of the\napplication\nin case of any problems with the\nstorages\n. To activate\nthis monitoring, the\napplication\nhas to register that callback function using\nara::\nper::RegisterRecoveryReportCallback\n.\n[SWS_PER_00480]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::RegisterRecoveryReportCallback\nis\ncalled,\nPersistency\nshall register the provided function and enable reporting of\nredundancy\nproblems in all\nstorages\nof this\napplication\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008)\n46 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\ntencyRedundancyHandlingScopeStorage\n,\nPersistency\nshall store the copies\nof the\nstorage\nin the different locations as follows:\n2\nThe first location contains the main copy, the second location contains all other\ncopies.\nn\n(==\nPersistencyRedundancyMOutOfN\n.\nn\n) Each copy is placed in a separate lo-\ncation.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008, RS_PER_00009, RS_PER_00010)\n[SWS_PER_00447]\nd\nIn case a\nPersistencyRedundancyHandling\naggregated\nas\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nredundancyHandling\nis derived as\nPersisten-\ncyRedundancyHash\n, the\nPersistency\nshall calculate a hash value when persisting\nthe\nstorage\nor an\nelement\nof the\nstorage\n(depending on\nPersistencyDeploy-\nment\n.\nredundancyHandling\n.\nscope\n), and shall use this hash value to check the\nstorage\nor the\nelement\nwhen it is read back.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008, RS_PER_00009,\nRS_PER_00010)\n[SWS_PER_00448]\nd\nPersistency\nshall calculate the hash value using the algo-\nrithm defined by\nPersistencyRedundancyHash\n.\nalgorithmFamily\nwith the bit\nwidth defined by\nPersistencyRedundancyHash\n.\nlength\n. If\nPersistencyRedun-\ndancyHash\n.\ninitializationVectorLength\nis configured, an initialization vector\nof this length shall be calculated containing random data and passed to the hash algo-\nrithm.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008, RS_PER_00009, RS_PER_00010)\nA possible approach to calculate the hash value and the random data would be to\nuse the\nCryptography\n[9]. The integration will have to take care that the con-\nfigured\nPersistencyRedundancyHash\n.\nlength\nand\nPersistencyRedundancy-\nHash\n.\ninitializationVectorLength\nare supported by the configured\nPersis-\ntencyRedundancyHash\n.\nalgorithmFamily\n.\n50 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P51_130",

      "source_page": 51,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2.6 Installation and Update of Persistent Data\nThe\nUpdate and Configuration Management\n[7] handles the life cycle of\nAdap-\ntive Applications\nwith the following phases:\n\u000f\nInstallation of new software\n\u000f\nUpdate of already installed software\n\u000f\nFinalization of updated software after the update succeeded\n\u000f\nRoll-back of updated software after the update failed\n\u000f\nRemoval of installed software\nFor all these phases,\npersistent data\nneeds to be handled alongside the appli-\ncation. The\nAdaptive Application\nmay trigger this handling explicitly by calling\nara::per::UpdatePersistency\nduring the verification phase that follows the in-\nstallation or update, or rely on the\nPersistency\nto do this implicitly when\nper-\nsistent data\nis accessed (\nara::per::OpenKeyValueStorage\n/\nara::per::\nOpenFileStorage\n). In both cases, the\nPersistency\nwill compare a previously\nstored\ncontract version\nand\ndeployment version\nagainst the\ncontract\nversion\nand\ndeployment version\nof the current\nmanifest\n, and perform the re-\nquired action.\nPersistency\nstores information about already installed\nstorages\ntogether with ver-\nsion information in a central location.\n[SWS_PER_00463]\nd\nPersistency\nshall store information about the installed\nKey-Value Storages\nand\nFile Storages\nin the location denoted by\nProcessToMachineMapping\n.\npersistencyCentralStorageURI\nof the\nPro-\ncessToMachineMapping\nthat refers to the\nProcess\nthat is referenced by\nPersis-\ntencyPortPrototypeToDeploymentMapping\ns. It shall also store the\ncontract\nversion\nand\ndeployment version\nof the current\nmanifest\nin this location.\nc\n(RS_-\nPER_00010, RS_PER_00012, RS_PER_00013, RS_PER_00014, RS_PER_00016)\n[SWS_PER_00469]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::UpdatePersistency\nis called, the\nPer-\nsistency\nshall follow [SWS_PER_00382] (for installation), [SWS_PER_00386] and\n[SWS_PER_00387] (for update), or [SWS_PER_00396] (for roll-back) for each\nstor-\nage\nconfigured as\nPersistencyDeployment\nin the deployment data.\nc\n(RS_PER_-\n00010, RS_PER_00012, RS_PER_00013, RS_PER_00014)\n[SWS_PER_00470]\nd\nWhen a\nKey-Value Storage\nis opened by the applica-\ntion using\nara::per::OpenKeyValueStorage\n, the\nPersistency\nshall follow\n[SWS_PER_00382] (for installation), [SWS_PER_00386] and [SWS_PER_00387] (for\nupdate), [SWS_PER_00446] (for finalization), or [SWS_PER_00396] (for roll-back) for\nthis\nKey-Value Storage\nconfigured as\nPersistencyKeyValueStorage\nin the\ndeployment data.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012, RS_PER_00013, RS_PER_-\n00014, RS_PER_00016)\n51 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P52_131",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00471",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 52,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_PER_00471]\nd\nWhen a\nFile Storage\nis opened by the\napplica-\ntion\nusing\nara::per::OpenFileStorage\n, the\nPersistency\nshall follow\n[SWS_PER_00382] (for installation), [SWS_PER_00386] and [SWS_PER_00387] (for\nupdate), [SWS_PER_00446] (for finalization), or [SWS_PER_00396] (for roll-back) for\neach\nFile Storage\nconfigured as\nPersistencyFileStorage\nin the deployment\ndata.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012, RS_PER_00013, RS_PER_00014, RS_-\nPER_00016)\n[SWS_PER_00378]\nd\nPersistency\nshall extract the\ncontract version\n(\nPersis-\ntencyInterface\n.\ncontractVersion\nor\nFunctionalClusterInteractsWith-\nPersistencyDeploymentMapping\n.\ncontractVersion\n) and the\ndeployment\nversion\n(\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nversion\n) from the\nmanifest\n, and store\nthem persistently in the location denoted by\nProcessToMachineMapping\n.\npersis-\ntencyCentralStorageURI\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00013, RS_PER_00014)\nThe\ncontract version\nis used by\nPersistency\nto detect a change of the ap-\nplication (see [SWS_PER_00387]), while the\ndeployment version\nis used to de-\ntect a change of the deployed\npersistent data\n(see [SWS_PER_00386] and\n[SWS_PER_00396]).\n[SWS_PER_CONSTR_00001]\nd\nWhen the\ncontract version\n(\nPersistencyIn-\nterface\n.\ncontractVersion\nor\nFunctionalClusterInteractsWithPersis-\ntencyDeploymentMapping\n.\ncontractVersion\n) is increased, the\ndeployment\nversion\n(\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nversion\n) needs to be increased, too.\nc\n(RS_-\nPER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\nThe\ndeployment version\nand\ncontract version\nare\nStrongRevisionLa-\nbelString\ns. These strings consists of a\nMajorVersion\n, a\nMinorVersion\n, a\nPatchVersion\n, and additional labels for pre-release versions and build information.\nIt is assumed that at least one of the first three will be incremented when the version is\nchanged, while the additional labels might be arbitrary.\n[SWS_PER_CONSTR_00002]\nd\nWhen the\ndeployment version\n(\nPersistency-\nDeployment\n.\nversion\n) or\ncontract version\n(\nPersistencyInterface\n.\ncon-\ntractVersion\nor\nFunctionalClusterInteractsWithPersistencyDeploy-\nmentMapping\n.\ncontractVersion\n) is increased, the\nMajorVersion\n,\nMinorVer-\nsion\n, or\nPatchVersion\nhave to be incremented.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_-\n00012)\nAfter installation of the\nAdaptive Application\n, the\nPersistency\nwill install pre-\ndefined\npersistent data\nfrom the\nmanifest\n. There are different possibilities how\nthis\npersistent data\ncan be defined in the\nmanifest\n:\n\u000f\nPersistent data\ncan be defined by an application designer within\nPersistencyKeyValueStorageInterface\nor\nPersistencyFileStor-\nageInterface\n.\n\u000f\nPersistent data\nthat was defined by an application designer can be changed\nand fine-tuned by an integrator within\nPersistencyKeyValueStorage\nor\nPersistencyFileStorage\n.\n52 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P53_132",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00379",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 53,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n\u000f\nPersistent data\ncan be directly defined by an integrator within\nPersisten-\ncyKeyValueStorage\nor\nPersistencyFileStorage\n.\n[SWS_PER_00379]\nd\nElements\ndefined in the deployment data (\nPersistencyDe-\nploymentElement\n) shall always be preferred over the\nelements\ndefined in the ap-\nplication design (\nPersistencyInterfaceElement\n). The latter shall only be used if\nthe former does not exist.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012, RS_PER_00013)\nAfter an update of the\nAdaptive Application\nor the\nmanifest\n, the\nPersis-\ntency\nwill create a backup of the\npersistent data\n, and then update the existing\npersistent data\nusing one of the following strategies:\n\u000f\nExisting\npersistent data\nis kept unchanged (\nkeepExisting\n).\n\u000f\nExisting\npersistent data\nis replaced (\noverwrite\n).\n\u000f\nExisting\npersistent data\nis removed (\ndelete\n).\n\u000f\nNew\npersistent data\nis added (\nkeepExisting\nand\noverwrite\n).\nThe update strategy can be set during application design or deployment, and can\nbe defined for the whole\nKey-Value Storage\nor\nFile Storage\n(\nPersistency-\nCollectionLevelUpdateStrategyEnum\n\nkeepExisting\nor\ndelete\n) and for a\nsingle\nkey-value pair\nor\nfile\n(\nPersistencyElementLevelUpdateStrate-\ngyEnum\n\nkeepExisting\n,\noverwrite\n, or\ndelete\n).\n[SWS_PER_00251]\nd\nAn update strategy defined in the deployment data (\nPersis-\ntencyDeploymentElement\n.\nupdateStrategy\n) shall always be preferred over the\nupdate strategy defined in the application design (\nPersistencyInterfaceEle-\nment\n.\nupdateStrategy\n). The latter shall only be used if the former does not exist.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012, RS_PER_00013)\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nupdateStrategy\nis a mandatory attribute and therefore\nPersistencyInterface\n.\nupdateStrategy\nis just a recommendation for the de-\nployment and never used by\nPersistency\n.\n[SWS_PER_00380]\nd\nAn update strategy defined for a single\nelement\n(\nPersisten-\ncyDeploymentElement\n.\nupdateStrategy\n,\nPersistencyInterfaceElement\n.\nupdateStrategy\n) shall always be preferred over the update strategy defined for\nthe enclosing\nstorage\n(\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nupdateStrategy\n,\nPersis-\ntencyInterface\n.\nupdateStrategy\n). The latter shall only be used if the former\ndoes not exist.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012, RS_PER_00013)\nWhen the update succeeded, the\nUpdate and Configuration Management\nwill\nfinalize the new\nAdaptive Application\n. The\nPersistency\nwill free the resources\nallocated by the last backup when it is opened the first time after the update succeeded.\nWhen the update failed, the\nUpdate and Configuration Management\nwill revert\nto the old\nAdaptive Application\nand/or\nmanifest\n. The\nPersistency\nwill then\nreplace the currently used\npersistent data\nby the backup created during the up-\ndate.\n53 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },

they\nwould have after installation of the\napplication\nusing the current\nmanifest\ninfor-\nmation.\nc\n(RS_PER_00009, RS_PER_00010, called,\nPersistency\nshall first check whether the\nkey-value pair\nis present in the\nman-\nifest\n, and otherwise return directly with\nkInitValueNotAvailable\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_-\n00009, RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\n[SWS_PER_00477]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::ResetKey\nis called\nfor a\nkey-value pair\nthat is present in the\nmanifest\n,\nPersistency\nshall reset\nthe given\nkey\nto the state it would have after installation of the\napplication\nusing the\ncurrent\nmanifest\ninformation.\nc\n(RS_PER_00009, RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\n[SWS_PER_00478]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::ResetAllFiles\nis called,\nPersistency\nshall reset the\nFile Storage\nto the state it would have after installation of the\nap-\nplication\nusing the current\nmanifest\ninformation.\nc\n(RS_PER_00009, RS_PER_-\n00010, RS_PER_00012)\n[SWS_PER_00573]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::ResetFile\nis called,\nPersistency\nshall first check whether RS_PER_00012)\n[SWS_PER_00479]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::ResetFile\nis called for a\nfile\nthat is present in the\nmanifest\n,\nPersistency\nshall reset the given\nfile\nto the\nstate it would have after installation of the\napplication\nusing the current\nmanifest\ninformation.\nc\n(RS_PER_00009, RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\nFinally, when the\nAdaptive Application\nis removed, the\nUpdate and Config-\nuration Management\nis responsible to remove the related\npersistent data\nas\nwell.\n7.2.6.1 Installation of Persistent Data\n[SWS_PER_00382]\nd\nWhen a\nstorage\nis opened by the\napplication\n, the\nPer-\nsistency\nshall check for the existence of any\npersistent data\nof this\nProcess\n.\n54 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

      "source_page": 55,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nIf no\npersistent data\nis found, the\nPersistency\nshall initialize the\npersistent\ndata\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\nInitialization of\npersistent data\nis described in paragraph 7.2.6.1.1 and paragraph\n7.2.6.1.2.\nTo be able to update\nPersistency\nwith changed\nredundancy\n,\nPersistency\nstores\nthe information about the used\nredundancy\nmeasures within the\nmetadata\nof each\nstorage\n. The same applies to the used keys and algorithms for encryption and au-\nthentication.\n[SWS_PER_00558]\nd\nWhen a new\nstorage\nis installed,\nPersistency\nshall store the\ninformation about the used\nredundancy\nin the\nmetadata\nof the\nstorage\n.\nc\n(RS_-\nPER_00008, RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\n[SWS_PER_00559]\nd\nWhen a new\nstorage\nis installed,\nPersistency\nshall store the\ninformation about keys and algorithms used for encryption and authentication in the\nmetadata\nof the\nstorage\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00005, RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\n7.2.6.1.1 Installation of Key-Value Storage\n[SWS_PER_00383]\nd\nPersistency\nshall create a\nKey-Value Storage\nfor each\nPortPrototype\ntyped by a\nPersistencyKeyValueStorageInterface\nthat is\nfound in the\nmanifest\nof a newly installed\nAdaptive Application\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_-\n00010, RS_PER_00012)\nThe\nKey-Value Storages\ncreated by [SWS_PER_00383] are identified at run-\ntime by the\nshortName\npath of the\nPortPrototype\n, passed as\nara::core::In-\nstanceSpecifier\nto\nara::per::OpenKeyValueStorage\n.\n[SWS_PER_00252]\nd\nPersistency\nshall create an entry in the\nKey-Value Stor-\nage\nfor each\nPersistencyKeyValueStorageInterface\n.\ndataElement\nand\nPersistencyKeyValueStorage\n.\nkeyValuePair\nthat is found in the\nmanifest\nof\na newly installed or updated\nAdaptive Application\n, and for which the update\nstrategy is not\ndelete\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\nKey-Value Storage\nentries are identified by the\nkey\n. An entry with identical\nkey\nmight be defined both in the\nPersistencyKeyValueStorageInterface\nas\ndataElement\nand the\nPersistencyKeyValueStorage\nas\nkeyValuePair\n, in\nwhich case [SWS_PER_00379] applies. The update strategy is determined accord-\ning to [SWS_PER_00251] and [SWS_PER_00380].\n[SWS_PER_00253]\nd\nEntries in the\nKey-Value Storage\nshall use the\nshortName\nof the\nPersistencyDataElement\nand/or\nPersistencyKeyValuePair\nas\nkey\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\n[SWS_PER_00254]\nd\nEntries in the\nKey-Value Storage\nshall be created with\nthe data type defined by the\nCppImplementationDataType\nwhich types the\nPersistencyDataElement\nand/or by the\nCppImplementationDataType\nrefer-\n55 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nenced as\nPersistencyKeyValuePair\n.\nvalueDataType\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_-\nPER_00012)\n[SWS_PER_00384]\nd\nEntries in the\nKey-Value Storage\nshall be created with the\nvalue taken from the\nPersistencyKeyValuePair\n.\ninitValue\nor, if that does\nnot exist, from the\nPersistencyDataRequiredComSpec\n.\ninitValue\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_-\n00010, RS_PER_00012)\n[SWS_PER_CONSTR_00003]\nd\nA\nmanifest\nis not valid if the value or data type of\nany\nPersistencyKeyValuePair\nor\nPersistencyDataElement\ncannot be deter-\nmined, or if the determined data types are conflicting.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_-\n00012)\nInvalid\nmanifests\nshould be rejected by the tooling.\n7.2.6.1.2 Installation of File Storage\n[SWS_PER_00385]\nd\nPersistency\nshall create a\nFile Storage\nfor each\nPort-\nPrototype\ntyped by a\nPersistencyFileStorageInterface\nthat is found in the\nmanifest\nof a newly installed\nAdaptive Application\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_-\nPER_00012)\nThe\nFile Storages\ncreated by [SWS_PER_00385] are identified at run-time by the\nshortName\npath of the\nPortPrototype\n, passed as\nara::core::InstanceSpec-\nifier\nto\nara::per::OpenFileStorage\n.\n[SWS_PER_00265]\nd\nPersistency\nshall create a\nfile\nin the\nFile Storage\nfor\neach\nPersistencyFileStorageInterface\n.\nfileElement\nand\nPersistency-\nFileStorage\n.\nfile\nthat is found in the\nmanifest\nof a newly installed or updated\nAdaptive Application\n, and for which the update strategy is not\ndelete\n.\nc\n(RS_-\nPER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\nThe\nfiles\nwithin a\nFile Storage\nare identified by their\nfile name\n. A\nfile\nwith\nthe same\nfile name\nmight be defined both in the\nPersistencyFileStorageIn-\nterface\nas\nfileElement\nand the\nPersistencyFileStorage\nas\nfile\n, in which\ncase [SWS_PER_00379] applies. The update strategy is determined according to\n[SWS_PER_00251] and [SWS_PER_00380].\n[SWS_PER_00266]\nd\nFiles\nin the\nFile Storage\nshall use the\nfile name\niden-\ntified by\nPersistencyFileElement\n.\nfileName\nand/or\nPersistencyFile\n.\nfile-\nName\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\n[SWS_PER_00267]\nd\nFiles\nin the\nFile Storage\nshall be created with the content\ntaken from the resource (within the installed\nSoftwarePackage\n) that is addressed\nby\nPersistencyFile\n.\ncontentUri\nor, if that does not exist, by\nPersistency-\nFileElement\n.\ncontentUri\n. If that does not exist either, an empty\nfile\nshall be\ncreated.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\n56 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P57_136",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_CONSTR_00004",

      "source_page": 57,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_PER_CONSTR_00004]\nd\nA\nmanifest\nis invalid if the\nshortName\ns of a\nPer-\nsistencyFileElement\nand a\nPersistencyFile\nwith the same\nfile name\ndif-\nfers.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\nInvalid\nmanifests\nshould be rejected by the tooling.\n7.2.6.2 Update of Persistent Data\n[SWS_PER_00386]\nd\nWhen a\nstorage\nis opened by the\napplication\n, the\nPer-\nsistency\nshall compare the\ndeployment version\n(\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nversion\n) in the\nmanifest\nagainst the stored\ndeployment version\n. If the\nde-\nployment version\nin the\nmanifest\nis higher than the stored\ndeployment ver-\nsion\n, the\nPersistency\nshall first create a backup of all the\npersistent data\nof\nthis\nProcess\nand then update the data.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00013)\nOnly one set of backup data needs to be kept at any time. When a new update is\nperformed, old backup data could be overwritten. Update of\npersistent data\nis\ndescribed in paragraph 7.2.6.2.1 and paragraph 7.2.6.2.2.\n[SWS_PER_00387]\nd\nIf the\napplication\nregistered a function using\nara::per::\nRegisterApplicationDataUpdateCallback\n, and if the\nPersistency\nhad\nto update at least one of its\nstorages\naccording to [SWS_PER_00386], it\nshall compare the\ncontract version\n(\nPersistencyInterface\n.\ncontractVer-\nsion\nor\nFunctionalClusterInteractsWithPersistencyDeploymentMap-\nping\n.\ncontractVersion\n) in the\nmanifest\nagainst the stored\ncontract version\n.\nIf the\ncontract version\nin the\nmanifest\nis higher than the stored\ncontract\nversion\n, the\nPersistency\nshall call the registered function for each\nstorage\nthat\nwas updated according to [SWS_PER_00386].\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00013)\nThe function registered by the\napplication\nusing\nara::per::RegisterAppli-\ncationDataUpdateCallback\ncan be used by the\napplication\nto update\nele-\nments\nof a\nstorage\nmanually. The\nstorage\nis identified by the\nara::core::In-\nstanceSpecifier\nprovided to this function. The\napplication\nmight then, based\non the\ncontract version\nof the stored data provided as second argument to the\nfunction, read in the stored data in the old format or with the old type, convert the data,\nand store it again with the new format or new type expected by the current\ncontract\nversion\n.\nExample: Version\n1\nof the\napplication\nstored the maximum speed in\nmph\nas\nuint8\n,\nbut version\n2\nexpects the maximum speed in\nkm=h\nas\nuint16\n.       "source_page": 61,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2.6.3 Finalization of Persistent Data after Successful Update\nAfter installation and update,\nPersistency\nwill usually be called with\nara::per::\nUpdatePersistency\nwithin the verification phase of the\napplication\n. When this\nsucceeded, the\napplication\nwill be finalized by\nUpdate and Configuration\nManagement\nand then started again in normal execution mode. In this case,\nPer-\nsistency\nmay remove any backups that were created during a preceding update.\nBecause\nPersistency\nhas different update strategies (all\nstorages\nwith\nara::\nper::UpdatePersistency\nor single\nstorages\nwith\nara::per::OpenKeyVal-\nueStorage\nand\nara::per::OpenFileStorage\n), it is also up to the\napplication\nto decide when the backup data shall be removed, by calling\nara::per::CleanUp-\nPersistency\n.\n[SWS_PER_00446]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::CleanUpPersistency\nis called by the\nap-\nplication\n, the\nPersistency\nshall remove all backup data of the\nstorage\n.\nc\n(RS_-\nPER_00016)\nUpdate of\npersistent data\nis described in subsubsection 7.2.6.2.\n7.2.6.4 Roll-Back of Persistent Data after Failed Update\n[SWS_PER_00396]\nd\nWhen a\nstorage\nis opened by the\napplication\n, the\nPer-\nsistency\nshall compare the\ndeployment version\n(\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nversion\n) in the\nmanifest\nagainst the stored\ndeployment version\n. If the\nde-\nployment version\nin the\nmanifest\nis lower than the stored\ndeployment ver-\nsion\n, the\nPersistency\nshall compare the\ndeployment version\nin the\nmanifest\nagainst the\ndeployment version\nstored in backup data. If the\ndeployment ver-\nsions\nmatch, the\nPersistency\nshall restore the backup. Otherwise, it shall remove\nall\nstorages\n, and re-install the\npersistent data\nfrom the\nmanifest\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_-\n00014)\nInitialization of\npersistent data\nis described in subsubsection 7.2.6.1.\n7.2.6.5 Removal of Persistent Data\nPersistency\nis not able to remove its own data when the\nUpdate and Config-\nuration Management\nremoves an\napplication\n, because the\napplication\nwill\nnot be executed in this case, and therefore\nPersistency\ndoes not run. On the other\nhand, the\nUpdate and Configuration Management\nmay use the information in\nthe\nmanifest\n(\nProcessToMachineMapping\n.\npersistencyCentralStorageURI\nand\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\ndeploymentUri\n) to obtain the locations of\nper-\nsistent data\n, and, if it has access to the locations, remove it.\n61 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P62_141",

      "source_page": 62,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2.7 Resource Management Concepts\nThe\nPersistency\nsupports configuration of both an upper and a lower limit for the\nresources used by a\nKey-Value Storage\nor a\nFile Storage\n.\nThe lower limit may already be defined by the application developer using\nPersisten-\ncyInterface\n.\nminimumSustainedSize\n. During deployment, the integrator may up-\ndate the lower limit using\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nminimumSustainedSize\nand\nadd an upper limit using\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nmaximumAllowedSize\n.\nThe\nPersistency\nwill actively monitor the upper limit, while the lower limit is ex-\npected to be checked during installation of the\nSoftwarePackage\nthat contains the\nExecutable\nwhich uses\nPersistency\n.\n[SWS_PER_00321]\nd\nThe\nPersistency\nshall ensure that the space actually allocated\nby a\nstorage\nnever surpasses the amount configured by\nPersistencyDeploy-\nment\n.\nmaximumAllowedSize\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00011)\nThis could be ensured by supervising all write accesses to\npersistent data\n. But\nthe implementation of the\nPersistency\nis free to chose other appropriate measures.\nThe\napplication\ncan also poll the amount of storage space currently occupied by a\ncomplete\nKey-Value Storage\nor\nFile Storage\nby using\nara::per::GetCur-\nrentKeyValueStorageSize\nor\nara::per::GetCurrentFileStorageSize\n, re-\nspectively. Naturally, the returned values will not drop below a configured minimum\nsize (\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nminimumSustainedSize\n) or rise above a config-\nured maximum size (\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nmaximumAllowedSize\n).\n[SWS_PER_00491]\nd\nara::per::GetCurrentKeyValueStorageSize\nshall re-\nturn the total size of the storage space currently allocated to a\nKey-Value Storage\n,\nincluding administrative data (apart from data stored in\nProcessToMachineMap-\nping\n.\npersistencyCentralStorageURI\n), redundant data, and backup data. The\nreported size may be inaccurate if the\nKey-Value Storage\nis currently open, or if an-\nother operation is currently being executed on the same\nstorage\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00011)\nThe inaccuracy is mainly due to the fact that\nmetadata\nof the\nstorage\nis only up-\ndated when the\nstorage\nis fully synchronized, and predicting the\nmetadata\nsize is\nsometimes very difficult.\n[SWS_PER_00492]\nd\nara::per::GetCurrentFileStorageSize\nshall return the\ntotal size of the storage space currently allocated to a\nFile Storage\n, including ad-\nministrative data (apart from data stored in\nProcessToMachineMapping\n.\npersis-\ntencyCentralStorageURI\n), all its\nfiles\n, redundant data, and backup data. The\nreported size may be inaccurate if the\nFile Storage\nis currently open, or if another\noperation is currently being executed on the same\nstorage\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00011)\n62 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
