      "source_page": 63,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.3 Key-Value Storage specific Features\nTo access a\nKey-Value Storage\n, the\napplication\nhas to call\nara::per::\nOpenKeyValueStorage\nwith the\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\nderived from\nthe\nmanifest\n(a\nshortName\npath from the\nExecutable\nto a\nPortPrototype\nor\na mapping derived from\nFunctionalClusterInteractsWithFunctionalClus-\nterMapping\n). This call will return an\nara::per::SharedHandle\nof an\nara::\nper::KeyValueStorage\n. The\nKey-Value Storage\nis closed when the\nara::\nper::SharedHandle\nand all of its copies go out of scope, or when\nara::core::\nDeinitialize\nis called.\n[SWS_PER_00506]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::OpenKeyValueStorage\nis called, and\nPersistency\nis properly initialized as described in [SWS_PER_00408],\nPersis-\ntency\nshall create a temporary storage that provides access to the\nKey-Value\nStorage\nidentified by the\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\n, and shall create\nand return an\nara::per::SharedHandle\nof an\nara::per::KeyValueStorage\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00002)\nIf\nara::per::OpenKeyValueStorage\nis called without proper initialization,\n[SWS_PER_00410] applies.\nAll operations on a\nKey-Value Storage\nwill be done in a temporary storage cre-\nated during the call to\nara::per::OpenKeyValueStorage\n, which the\napplica-\ntion\ncan persist using\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SyncToStorage\n, or re-\nset to the last stored state with\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::DiscardPend-\ningChanges\n.\nTherefore, if the\nKey-Value Storage\nis just destructed (also implicitly when the\nProcess\nterminates), the\nKey-Value Storage\nis not updated, and the next time the\nKey-Value Storage\nis accessed, the\napplication\nwill see the last saved state.\n[SWS_PER_00331]\nd\nModifications of a\nKey-Value Storage\nthat have not been per-\nsisted with a call to\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SyncToStorage\nshall be dis-\ncarded when the\nKey-Value Storage\nis closed or the system is restarted, just as\nif\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::DiscardPendingChanges\nhad been called.\nc\n(RS_PER_00003)\nChanges done by any thread (using a copy of the\nara::per::SharedHandle\n) will\nbe immediately visible in all other threads. This also applies to\nara::per::KeyVal-\nueStorage::DiscardPendingChanges\n, which resets the\nkey-value pairs\nin\nall threads, and to\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SyncToStorage\n, which per-\nsists all changes done by any thread.\n[SWS_PER_00494]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SyncToStorage\nis\ncalled,\nPersistency\nshall store all changes permanently that have been done to\nthe\nKey-Value Storage\nsince the last call to this method or since the\nKey-Value\nStorage\nwas opened.\nPersistency\nshall also update any configured\nredundancy\nwithin this call.\nc\n(RS_PER_00001)\n63 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

      "source_page": 64,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nPlease note that depending on the implementation of\nPersistency\n, the configuration\nof an optionally used file system, and the capabilities of the used physical storage\ndevice, the actual storage of\nkey-value pairs\nmay be delayed. So, in case of an\nimmediate power down directly after this call, the physical data may be updated only\npartially or not at all. Therefore, data may be lost or, without\nredundancy\n, data may\neven be corrupted in this case.\nThe handling of\nredundancy\nis described in detail in subsection 7.2.5.\n[SWS_PER_00495]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::DiscardPend-\ningChanges\nis called,\nPersistency\nshall reset the\nKey-Value Storage\nto\nthe last persisted state, which is the state after the last call to\nara::per::Key-\nValueStorage::SyncToStorage\nor after opening the\nKey-Value Storage\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00001)\nSingle\nkey-value pairs\nof the\nKey-Value Storage\nare accessed using\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetValue\nand\nara::per::KeyValueStor-\nage::SetValue\n.\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SetValue\nmay also be used\nto create a\nkey-value pair\n.\n[SWS_PER_00496]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetValue\nis called,\nPersistency\nshall first check whether the\nkey-value pair\nis present in the tem-\nporary storage, and otherwise return directly with\nkKeyNotFound\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00002,\nRS_PER_00003)\n[SWS_PER_00497]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetValue\nis called\nfor an existing\nkey-value pair\n,\nPersistency\nshall check whether the tem-\nplated data type matches the stored data type, and otherwise return directly with\nkDataTypeMismatch\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00002, RS_PER_00003)\n[SWS_PER_00498]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetValue\nis called\nfor an existing\nkey-value pair\nwith the correct templated data type,\nPersistency\nshall return the stored\nvalue\nof the\nkey-value pair\n, or, if the\nvalue\nwas recently\nchanged by\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SetValue\n(also in another thread),\nthis new temporary\nvalue\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00002, RS_PER_00003)\n[SWS_PER_00499]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SetValue\nis called\nfor an existing\nkey-value pair\n,\nPersistency\nshall check whether the tem-\nplated data type matches the stored data type, and otherwise return directly with\nkDataTypeMismatch\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00001, RS_PER_00003)\n[SWS_PER_00534]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SetValue\nis called\nfor an existing\nkey-value pair\nwith the correct templated data type,\nPersistency\nshall store the new\nvalue\nof the\nkey-value pair\nin the temporary storage.\nc\n(RS_-\nPER_00001, RS_PER_00003)\n[SWS_PER_00501]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SetValue\nis called,\nand the\nkey-value pair\ndoes not exist in the temporary storage,\nPersistency\nshall create the\nkey-value pair\nwith the templated data type and the provided\nvalue\nin the temporary storage.\nc\n(RS_PER_00001, RS_PER_00003)\n64 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

      "source_page": 65,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nTo remove a single\nkey-value pair\n, the\napplication\nmay use\nara::\nper::KeyValueStorage::RemoveKey\n, while\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::\nRemoveAllKeys\nempties the\nKey-Value Storage\n. The type of a\nkey-value\npair\nmay be changed by first removing it, and then creating it with the new type.\n[SWS_PER_00502]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::RemoveKey\nis\ncalled,\nPersistency\nshall first check whether the\nkey-value pair\nis present\nin the temporary storage, and otherwise return directly with\nkKeyNotFound\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00001, RS_PER_00003)\n[SWS_PER_00535]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::RemoveKey\nis called\nfor an existing\nkey-value pair\n,\nPersistency\nshall remove the\nkey-value pair\nfrom the temporary storage.\nc\n(RS_PER_00001, RS_PER_00003)\n[SWS_PER_00503]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::RemoveAllKeys\nis\ncalled,\nPersistency\nshall remove all\nkey-value pairs\nfrom the temporary stor-\nage, resulting in an empty\nKey-Value Storage\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00001)\nFinally, the\napplication\ncan check for the existence of a single\nkey\nwith\nara::\nper::KeyValueStorage::KeyExists\n, check the current size of a\nvalue\nusing\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetCurrentValueSize\n, and acquire a list of all\ncurrently available\nkeys\nusing\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetAllKeys\n.\n[SWS_PER_00504]\nd\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::KeyExists\nshall return\ntrue if the\nkey\nis present in the temporary storage, otherwise it shall return false.\nc\n(RS_PER_00003)\n[SWS_PER_00565]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetCurrentVal-\nueSize\nis called,\nPersistency\nshall first check whether the\nkey-value pair\nis present in the temporary\nstorage\n, and otherwise return directly with\nkKeyNot-\nFound\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00003)\n[SWS_PER_00566]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetCurrentVal-\nueSize\nis called for an existing\nkey-value pair\n,\nPersistency\nshall return the\ncurrent size of its\nvalue\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00003)\n[SWS_PER_00505]\nd\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetAllKeys\nshall return\nan\nara::core::Vector\nof\nara::core::String\n, containing all the\nkeys\nthat are\npresent in the temporary storage.       "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4 File Storage specific Features\nTo access a\nFile Storage\n, the\napplication\nhas to call\nara::per::Open-\nFileStorage\nwith the\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\nderived from the\nman-\nifest\n(a\nshortName\npath from the\nExecutable\nto a\nPortPrototype\nor a\nmapping derived from\nFunctionalClusterInteractsWithFunctionalClus-\nterMapping\n).       "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nThe\nfile\nis closed when the\nara::per::UniqueHandle\ngoes out of scope, or when\nara::core::Deinitialize\nis called.\n[SWS_PER_00457]\nd\nWhen a\nfile\nis closed,\nPersistency\nshall ensure that all\nchanges to the\nfile\nare persisted. This does not need to be done immediately like\nwhen\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::SyncToFile\nis called, but may happen\nat a later time, latest when the\nfile\nis opened again, or\nara::core::Deinitial-\nize\nis called.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nSome of the overloads of the\nfile\nopening functions receive an\nara::per::Open-\nMode\nas an argument. OpenModes can be combined using the operators | and |=.\n[SWS_PER_00514]\nd\nara::per::operator\n| and\nara::per::operator\n|=\ntake two\nara::per::OpenMode\narguments and return the combined\nara::per::\nOpenMode\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nAll\nfiles\nof\nPersistency\nare implicitly readable, even when opened as \"write only\",\nwhich is expressed by\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor\ninheriting from\nara::\nper::ReadAccessor\n. The\nara::per::ReadAccessor\nclass consequently also\noffers the methods related to\nfile\npositions.\n[SWS_PER_00515]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::SetPosition\nshall set the\nfile\nposition to the provided position. If the provided position is located outside of\nthe current content of the\nfile\n(including the position at the end of the\nfile\n),\nara::\nper::ReadAccessor::SetPosition\nshall keep the previous\nfile\nposition and re-\nturn\nkInvalidPosition\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00516]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::MovePosition\nshall move the\nfile\nposition to offset bytes according to the provided origin. If the new position would\nbe located outside of the current content of the\nfile\n(including the position at the end\nof the\nfile\n),\nara::per::ReadAccessor::MovePosition\nshall keep the previous\nfile\nposition and return\nkInvalidPosition\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00517]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::GetPosition\nshall return the\ncurrent read/write position in the\nfile\n. In the case of an empty\nfile\n, the position\nshall be returned as\n0\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00518]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::IsEof\nshall return true if the\nposition is the last possible position in the\nfile\n, otherwise false.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nara::per::ReadAccessor::IsEof\nwill return true if the current position corre-\nsponds to the total\nfile\nsize, which can be obtained separately using\nara::per::\nReadAccessor::GetSize\n. In other words, true is only returned when the current\nposition is at the position directly after the last character in the\nfile\n, or if the\nfile\nis\nempty.\n[SWS_PER_00519]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::GetSize\nshall return the cur-\nrent total size of the\nfile\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nPersistency\ndoes not care whether the content of a\nfile\nis text or some binary\ndata, and therefore offers separate methods to access the\nfile\ncontent as text or as\n69 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nbinary data. To read content from a text\nfile\n, the\napplication\nmay use one of the\nfollowing methods of the\nara::per::ReadAccessor\nclass:\n[SWS_PER_00520]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::PeekChar\nshall return the\ncharacter at the current\nfile\nposition without changing the position.\nc\n(RS_PER_-\n00004)\n[SWS_PER_00521]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::GetChar\nshall return the char-\nacter at the current\nfile\nposition and advance the position by one.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00522]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::ReadText\nshall read the text\nfrom the current position to the end of the\nfile\nand return it as an\nara::core::\nString\n. The position shall be set to the end of the\nfile\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00523]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::ReadText\nshall read the\nn\ncharacters of text from the current position and return them as an\nara::core::\nString\n. The position shall be incremented by\nn\n. In case the end of the\nfile\nis\nreached during this operation, the available characters shall be returned, and the posi-\ntion shall be set to the end of the\nfile\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00524]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::ReadLine\nshall read all char-\nacters until the delimiter (defaulting to the newline character) or the end of the\nfile\nis reached, and return them as a\nara::core::String\n. The delimiter shall not be\nincluded in the returned\nara::core::String\n. The position shall be set to the char-\nacter following the delimiter or the end of the\nfile\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004, RS_AP_00136)\nAll these methods return characters with a size of eight bits, which are just so-called\ncode units\nin case of\nUTF-8\n, not\ncode points\n. Therefore, these methods might\nreturn incomplete\ncode points\n.\nPersistency\nitself does not change or interpret\nthe content of a\nfile\nwhen accessing it in text mode. It is assumed, though, that\nfiles\nin the\nFile Storage\nare encoded as\nUTF-8\n(see [RS_AP_00136]). It is also\nassumed that line endings are handled according to\nUNIX\nconventions, i.e. just\nLF\n(\"\n\\n\n\").\n[SWS_PER_CONSTR_00006]\nd\nIf a\nCppImplementationDataType\nwith\ncategory\nequal to\nSTRING\nis used as\nPersistencyDataElement\n, then the encoding of this\nstring\ndata type is expected to be\nUTF-8\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00003, RS_PER_00004, RS_-\nAP_00136)\nThis means that a\nCppImplementationDataType\ncan only be mapped to an\nApplicationDataType\nof\ncategory STRING\nwhere attribute\nswDataDefProps\n.\nswTextProps\n.\nbaseType\n.\nbaseTypeDefinition\n.\nbaseTypeEncoding\nis set to the\nvalue\nUTF-8\nas defined by [constr_5035]. If a\nCppImplementationDataType\nwith-\nout an\nApplicationDataType\nis used there is no formal description about the\nUTF-\n8\nencoding in the\nServiceInterface\ndescription.\nThe following methods of the\nara::per::ReadAccessor\nclass can be used by an\napplication\nto read binary content from a file:\n[SWS_PER_00525]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::PeekByte\nshall return the byte\nat the current\nfile\nposition without changing the position.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n70 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_PER_00526]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::GetByte\nshall return the byte\nat the current\nfile\nposition and advance the position by one.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00527]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::ReadBinary\nshall read binary\ndata from the current position to the end of the\nfile\nand return it as an\nara::core::\nVector\nof\nara::core::Byte\n. The position shall be set to the end of the\nfile\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00528]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::ReadBinary\nshall read the\nn\ncharacters of text from the current position and return them as an\nara::core::Vec-\ntor\nof\nara::core::Byte\n. The position shall be incremented by\nn\n. In case the end\nof the\nfile\nis reached during this operation, the available bytes shall be returned, and\nthe position shall be set to the end of the\nfile\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nTo write text to\nfiles\n, the\napplication\nmay use the\nara::per::ReadWriteAc-\ncessor::WriteText\nmethod or the\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::opera-\ntor\n<< of the\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor\nclass, which treat text in the same\nway as described above for e.g.\nara::per::ReadAccessor::ReadText\n.\n[SWS_PER_00557]\nd\nIf the\nfile\nwas opened with\nara::per::OpenMode\nset to\nkAppend\n,\nPersistency\nshall always set the current position to the end of the\nfile\nbefore writing data to the\nfile\naccording to [SWS_PER_00529], [SWS_PER_00530],\nor [SWS_PER_00531].\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00529]\nd\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::WriteText\nshall write\nthe characters provided as\nara::core::StringView\nto the\nfile\nat the current\nposition, possibly overwriting current content and advancing the end of the\nfile\nif\nnecessary. The position shall be set to the character following the last character that\nwas written during this operation, or to the end of the\nfile\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00530]\nd\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::operator\n<< shall write\nthe characters provided as\nara::core::StringView\nto the\nfile\nat the current po-\nsition, possibly overwriting current content and advancing the end of the\nfile\nif nec-\nessary. The position shall be set to the character following the last character that was\nwritten during this operation, or to the end of the\nfile\n. If an error occurs during this\noperation, the\nfile\ncontent might be partially updated and the resulting\nfile\nposition\nmight not be as expected.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nTo write binary data to a\nfile\n, the\napplication\nmay use the method\nara::per::\nReadWriteAccessor::WriteBinary\nof the\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor\nclass. The position shall be set to the byte following the last byte that was\nwritten during this operation, or to the end of the\nfile\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nThe\napplication\nmay use\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::SetFileSize\nto\nexplicitly set the\nfile\nsize to a defined value in order to truncate a\nfile\nor to empty\n71 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

      "source_page": 72,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nit. Enlarging\nfiles\nis not supported by\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::Set-\nFileSize\n.\n[SWS_PER_00532]\nd\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::SetFileSize\nshall set\nthe\nfile\nsize to the provided value. The read/write position shall be set to the end of\nthe\nfile\nif the current position is higher than the new\nfile\nsize. If the provided value\nis larger than the current\nfile\nsize,\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::SetFile-\nSize\nshall return\nkInvalidSize\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nWhen the\napplication\nchanged a\nfile\n,\nPersistency\nwill ensure that these\nchanges are persisted. This can happen at any time, and latest when the\nfile\nis closed. To trigger an additional synchronization of the\nfile\ncontent to the per-\nsistent storage, the\napplication\nmay call\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::\nSyncToFile\n.\n[SWS_PER_00533]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::SyncToFile\nis\ncalled,\nPersistency\nshall store the content of the\nfile\n.\nPersistency\nshall also\nupdate any configured\nredundancy\nwithin this call.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nPlease note that depending on the implementation of\nPersistency\n, the configuration\nof an optionally used file system, and the capabilities of the used physical storage\ndevice, the actual storage of the\nfile\ncontent may be delayed. So, in case of an\nimmediate power down directly after this call, the physical data may be updated only\npartially or not at all. Therefore, data may be lost or, without\nredundancy\n, data may\neven be corrupted in this case.\nThe handling of\nredundancy\nis described in detail in subsection 7.2.5.\n7.4.1 Access to Additional Information about Files\nTo gain information about stored\nfiles\n, the\nPersistency\nprovides the\nmethods\nara::per::FileStorage::GetCurrentFileSize\nand\nara::per::\nFileStorage::GetFileInfo\n.\nThe\napplication\ncan poll the amount of storage space currently occupied by a single\nfile\nusing\nara::per::FileStorage::GetCurrentFileSize\nof an open\nFile\nStorage\n.\n[SWS_PER_00549]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::GetCurrentFileSize\nis\ncalled,\nPersistency\nshall first check whether the\nfile\nis present in the\nFile Stor-\nage\n, and otherwise return directly with\nkFileNotFound\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\n[SWS_PER_00493]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::GetCurrentFileSize\nis\ncalled for an existing\nfile\n,\nPersistency\nshall return the current size of the passed\nfile\n. This size shall reflect only the data contained in the\nfile\n. In case the\nfile\nis\ncurrently open,\nPersistency\nshall return the current size of the\nfile\n, which might\ndiffer from the size of the\nfile\nin the\nstorage\nif the last changes are not yet synchro-\nnized. Otherwise, if the\nfile\nis not open,\nPersistency\nshall return the size of any\n72 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P73_152",

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nexisting instance of the\nfile\nwithout checking the consistency/validity of the\nfile\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00011)\nPlease note that administrative and redundant information is not included in the\nfile\nsize reported by\nara::per::FileStorage::GetCurrentFileSize\n, while it is in-\ncluded in the total size of the\nFile Storage\nreturned by\nara::per::GetCurrent-\nFileStorageSize\n(see [SWS_PER_00492]).\nUsing\nara::per::FileStorage::GetFileInfo\n, the\napplication\ncan acquire\ninformation about the time the\nfile\nwas created (\ncreationTime\n), last modified (\nmodificationTime\n), and last accessed (\naccessTime\n), and how and by whom it\nwas created (\nfileCreationState\n) and last modified (\nfileModificationState\n).\n[SWS_PER_00550]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::GetFileInfo\nis called,\nPersistency\nshall first check whether the\nfile\nis present in the\nFile Storage\n,\nand otherwise return directly with\nkFileNotFound\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\n[SWS_PER_00440]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::GetFileInfo\nis called for\nan existing but currently not opened\nfile\n,\nPersistency\nshall gather the required\ninformation from any existing instance of the\nfile\n(without checking the consistency/-\nvalidity of this\nfile\n) into a\nara::per::FileInfo\nstruct and return it to the\nappli-\ncation\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00570]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::GetFileInfo\nis called for\nan existing and currently opened\nfile\n,\nPersistency\nshall return the time when the\nfile\nwas opened for\naccessTime\nand\ncreationTime\n(the latter only if the\nfile\nwas also created at the same time).\nFor the\nmodificationTime\n, before the\napplication\nwrote anything to the\nfile\n,\nPersistency\nshall return the original modification time. Afterwards,\nPersistency\nshall return the time the\nfile\nwas last modified by the\napplication\nor\nara::per::\nReadWriteAccessor::SyncToFile\nwas last called.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nIn case the\nPersistency\nuses a file system of the underlying OS, part of that infor-\nmation (like the creation or access time) can be obtained from the file system. Please\nnote that the time stamps returned by\nara::per::FileStorage::GetFileInfo\non a closed\nfile\nmight be later than the ones returned by\nPersistency\nwhile the\nfile\nwas still opened, because\nPersistency\nhas no control over the actual point in\ntime at which a file system (if used) updates these time stamps.\n[SWS_PER_00458]\nd\nIf\ncreationTime\n,\nmodificationTime\n, or\naccessTime\nare\nnot available, they shall be set to\n0\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nAs an example, the\naccessTime\nis not available for a read-only\nFile Storage\n, and\nwould therefore be reported as midnight 1970-01-01.\n73 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n8 API Specification\nThe APIs for accessing\nFile Storages\nand\nKey-Value Storage\nare completely\nseparate, and therefore divided into separate sections. Additional sections describe\ncommon functionality.\nThe API of\nPersistency\nis designed around the\nara::per::SharedHandle\nand\nara::per::UniqueHandle\n, which are returned by factory functions like\nara::\nper::OpenKeyValueStorage\nor\nara::per::FileStorage::OpenFileRead-\nWrite\n. The classes defined in this chapter cannot be constructed directly by the\nAdaptive Application\n, and consequently the default constructors are considered\nto be not publicly accessible (i.e. to be deleted, private, or protected).\n8.1 General Features of Persistency\n8.1.1 ara::core Types\nThe\nara::per\nAPI is based heavily on the\nara::core\ntypes defined in [2].\nara::core::Result\nis used wherever possible, and because of this, most methods\nare defined as\nnoexcept\n.\nConsequently, in situations where memory cannot be allocated for new objects, the\nPersistency\nshall terminate the process by calling\nara::core::Abort\n(see [2]).\n74 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

It allows to monitor these operations with a callback function installed with\nara::per::RegisterApplicationDataUpdateCallback\n.       "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n8.2 Key-Value Storage\nThis section lists all functions and classes that are required to operate a\nKey-Value\nStorage\n.\nThe following functions are used to get access to a\nKey-Value Storage\n, to recover\nas much as possible after it was corrupted, to reset it to the deployed defaults, and to\nget the amount of storage space allocated to the\nKey-Value Storage\n.\n8.2.1 OpenKeyValueStorage\n[SWS_PER_00052] Definition of API function ara::per::OpenKeyValueStorage\nd"
    },

      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P98_246",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00052",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 98,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "The shortName path of a PortPrototype typed by a PersistencyKey\nValueStorageInterface."

    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P98_247",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00052",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 98,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Returned if the passed InstanceSpecifier does not match any\nPersistencyKeyValueStorageInterface configured for this\nExecutable."

      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00052",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 98,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Returned if UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, or Reset\nPersistency is currently being executed, or if RecoverKeyValue\nStorage or ResetKeyValueStorage is currently being executed for\nthe same Key-Value Storage."
    },

      "source_page": 99,

      "source_page": 114,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n8.3 File Storage\nThis section lists all functions and classes that are required to operate a\nFile Stor-\nage\n.\nThe following functions are used to get access to a\nFile Storage\n, to recover as\nmuch as possible after it was corrupted, to reset it to the deployed defaults, and to get\nthe amount of storage space allocated to the\nFile Storage\n. In addition, operators\nare present to combine the\nara::per::OpenMode\nvalues passed as\nmode\nto the\nOpenFile\n*\nfunctions.\n8.3.1 OpenFileStorage\n[SWS_PER_00116] Definition of API function ara::per::OpenFileStorage\nd"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P114_327",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00116",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 114,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "The shortName path of a PortPrototype typed by a PersistencyFile\nStorageInterface."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P114_328",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00116",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 114,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Returned if the passed InstanceSpecifier does not match any\nPersistencyFileStorageInterface configured for this Executable."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P114_329",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00116",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 114,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Returned if UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, or Reset\nPersistency is currently being executed, or if RecoverAllFiles or\nResetAllFiles is currently being executed for the same File Storage."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P114_330",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00116",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 114,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "5\n114 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P115_331",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00335",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 115,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P115_332",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00335",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 115,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Opens a File Storage.\nOpenFileStorage will fail with kResourceBusy when the File Storage is currently being modified\nby a call from another thread to UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, ResetPersistency,\nRecoverAllFiles, or ResetAllFiles.\nBecause multiple threads can access the same File Storage concurrently, the File Storage might\nnot be closed when the SharedHandle returned by this function goes out of scope. It will only be\nclosed when all SharedHandles that refer to the same File Storage went out of scope."
    },

      "verbatim_text": "Writes the content of a StringView to the file.\nThe time when the content is persisted depends on the implementation of Persistency.   "bisheriges_fragment": "<div class=\"ai module-guide\"><p class=\"ai-note\">Automatisch generierte Beschreibung, inhaltlich abgeleitet aus den referenzierten AUTOSAR-R25-11-Dokumenten (SWS-Spezifikation und begleitende Standarddokumente) — kein offizieller AUTOSAR-Text. Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h4>Zweck und Systemgrenze</h4><p><code>ara::per</code> macht konfigurierte persistente Daten für Adaptive Applications zugänglich. Das Modell unterscheidet Key-Value Storages als Mengen typisierter Schlüssel-Wert-Paare und File Storages als Mengen benannter Dateien; beide können pro Anwendung kombiniert werden. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=section.7.1\">SWS Persistency §7.1 „The Architecture of Persistency“</a></p><p>Die Storage-Instanz ist nicht frei wählbar, sondern wird durch einen <code>ara::core::InstanceSpecifier</code> auf eine manifestierte Persistency-Schnittstelle bezogen. Zugriffsrechte können read-only, read/write, write-only oder – für Anwendungen – write-only-once sein. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.1\">SWS Persistency §7.1.1 „Configuration of Persistency“</a></p><h4>Entscheidung: Schlüssel oder Datei</h4><p>Wähle <code>KeyValueStorage</code> für adressierbare, typisierte Zustände mit einer expliziten Synchronisierungsgrenze; wähle <code>FileStorage</code> für dateiförmige Inhalte und Accessor-basiertes Lesen bzw. Schreiben. Initialwerte und initiale Dateien können mit Installation oder Update mitgeliefert werden. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.2\">SWS Persistency §7.1.2 „Configuration of Key-Value Storages“</a> <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.3\">SWS Persistency §7.1.3 „Configuration of File Storages“</a></p><p class=\"interp\"><strong>Interpretation:</strong> Die Auswahl ist ein Datenmodell-Entscheid: kleine, logisch getrennte Zustände profitieren von Schlüsseln; zusammenhängende oder streamartige Inhalte passen eher zur Datei-Schnittstelle. Sie folgt aus den unterschiedlichen, in der Spezifikation beschriebenen Zugriffsmodellen.</p><h4>Betriebsmodell und Datenhaltbarkeit</h4><p>Ein geöffneter Key-Value Storage arbeitet zunächst auf temporären Daten. <code>SyncToStorage</code> schreibt alle Änderungen seit Öffnen oder letzter Synchronisierung dauerhaft und aktualisiert konfigurierte Redundanz; ohne Synchronisierung werden Änderungen beim Schließen oder Neustart verworfen. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=section.7.3\">SWS Persistency §7.3 „Key-Value Storage specific Features“</a></p><p>Bei Dateien wird die konkrete Datei über einen Accessor geöffnet. Schreibzugriffe können über <code>SyncToFile</code> gezielt in den physischen Speicher übertragen werden; Ownership des Accessors ist exklusiv. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=section.7.4\">SWS Persistency §7.4 „File Storage specific Features“</a></p><h4>Schutz, Wiederherstellung und Ressourcen</h4><p>Redundanz kann Integrität über Prüfsummen oder mehrere Kopien absichern; bei nicht behebbaren Befunden kann ein Recovery-Report-Callback die Anwendung informieren. Eine Wiederherstellung kann initiale oder ältere Daten ergeben und ist daher fachlich zu prüfen. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.2.4\">SWS Persistency §7.2.4 „Redundancy Concepts“</a></p><p>Der konfigurierte Höchstwert begrenzt tatsächlich belegten Speicher. Die Größenabfragen enthalten Metadaten sowie Redundanz- und Backupbedarf und können bei offenem Storage oder parallelen Operationen ungenau sein. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.2.6\">SWS Persistency §7.2.6 „Resource Management Concepts“</a></p><h4>Installation, Update und Rollback</h4><p>Die Target Configuration kann vordefinierte Werte und Dateien einbringen. Während der Verifikationsphase kann <code>UpdatePersistency</code> Änderungen nach neuen Konfigurationsdaten ausführen; nach erfolgreicher Finalisierung entfernt <code>CleanUpPersistency</code> Sicherungsdaten. Ist eine ältere Konfiguration aktiviert, erfolgt abhängig von der gespeicherten Backupversion eine Wiederherstellung oder Neuinstallation. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.2.5\">SWS Persistency §7.2.5 „Installation and Update of Persistent Data“</a></p><div <div class="ai module-guide"><p class="ai-note">Automatisch generierte Beschreibung, inhaltlich abgeleitet aus den referenzierten AUTOSAR-R25-11-Dokumenten (SWS-Spezifikation und begleitende Standarddokumente) — kein offizieller AUTOSAR-Text. Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h4>Zweck und Systemgrenze</h4><p><code>ara::per</code> macht konfigurierte persistente Daten für Adaptive Applications zugänglich. Das Modell unterscheidet Key-Value Storages als Mengen typisierter Schlüssel-Wert-Paare und File Storages als Mengen benannter Dateien; beide können pro Anwendung kombiniert werden. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=section.7.1">SWS Persistency §7.1 „The Architecture of Persistency“</a></p><p>Die Storage-Instanz ist nicht frei wählbar, sondern wird durch einen <code>ara::core::InstanceSpecifier</code> auf eine manifestierte Persistency-Schnittstelle bezogen. Zugriffsrechte können read-only, read/write, write-only oder – für Anwendungen – write-only-once sein. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.1">SWS Persistency §7.1.1 „Configuration of Persistency“</a></p><h4>Entscheidung: Schlüssel oder Datei</h4><p>Wähle <code>KeyValueStorage</code> für adressierbare, typisierte Zustände mit einer expliziten Synchronisierungsgrenze; wähle <code>FileStorage</code> für dateiförmige Inhalte und Accessor-basiertes Lesen bzw. Schreiben. Initialwerte und initiale Dateien können mit Installation oder Update mitgeliefert werden. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.2">SWS Persistency §7.1.2 „Configuration of Key-Value Storages“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.3">SWS Persistency §7.1.3 „Configuration of File Storages“</a></p><p class="interp"><strong>Interpretation:</strong> Die Auswahl ist ein Datenmodell-Entscheid: kleine, logisch getrennte Zustände profitieren von Schlüsseln; zusammenhängende oder streamartige Inhalte passen eher zur Datei-Schnittstelle. Sie folgt aus den unterschiedlichen, in der Spezifikation beschriebenen Zugriffsmodellen.</p><h4>Betriebsmodell und Datenhaltbarkeit</h4><p>Ein geöffneter Key-Value Storage arbeitet zunächst auf temporären Daten. <code>SyncToStorage</code> schreibt alle Änderungen seit Öffnen oder letzter Synchronisierung dauerhaft und aktualisiert konfigurierte Redundanz; ohne Synchronisierung werden Änderungen beim Schließen oder Neustart verworfen. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=section.7.3">SWS Persistency §7.3 „Key-Value Storage specific Features“</a></p><p>Bei Dateien wird die konkrete Datei über einen Accessor geöffnet. Schreibzugriffe können über <code>SyncToFile</code> gezielt in den physischen Speicher übertragen werden; Ownership des Accessors ist exklusiv. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=section.7.4">SWS Persistency §7.4 „File Storage specific Features“</a></p><h4>Schutz, Wiederherstellung und Ressourcen</h4><p>Redundanz kann Integrität über Prüfsummen oder mehrere Kopien absichern; bei nicht behebbaren Befunden kann ein Recovery-Report-Callback die Anwendung informieren. Eine Wiederherstellung kann initiale oder ältere Daten ergeben und ist daher fachlich zu prüfen. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.2.4">SWS Persistency §7.2.4 „Redundancy Concepts“</a></p><p>Der konfigurierte Höchstwert begrenzt tatsächlich belegten Speicher. Die Größenabfragen enthalten Metadaten sowie Redundanz- und Backupbedarf und können bei offenem Storage oder parallelen Operationen ungenau sein. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.2.6">SWS Persistency §7.2.6 „Resource Management Concepts“</a></p><h4>Installation, Update und Rollback</h4><p>Die Target Configuration kann vordefinierte Werte und Dateien einbringen. Während der Verifikationsphase kann <code>UpdatePersistency</code> Änderungen nach neuen Konfigurationsdaten ausführen; nach erfolgreicher Finalisierung entfernt <code>CleanUpPersistency</code> Sicherungsdaten. Ist eine ältere Konfiguration aktiviert, erfolgt abhängig von der gespeicherten Backupversion eine Wiederherstellung oder Neuinstallation. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.2.5">SWS Persistency §7.2.5 „Installation and Update of Persistent Data“</a></p><div Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h4>Zweck und Systemgrenze</h4><p><code>ara::per</code> macht konfigurierte persistente Daten für Adaptive Applications zugänglich. Das Modell unterscheidet Key-Value Storages als Mengen typisierter Schlüssel-Wert-Paare und File Storages als Mengen benannter Dateien; beide können pro Anwendung kombiniert werden. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=section.7.1">SWS Persistency §7.1 „The Architecture of Persistency“</a></p><p>Die Storage-Instanz ist nicht frei wählbar, sondern wird durch einen <code>ara::core::InstanceSpecifier</code> auf eine manifestierte Persistency-Schnittstelle bezogen. Zugriffsrechte können read-only, read/write, write-only oder – für Anwendungen – write-only-once sein. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.1">SWS Persistency §7.1.1 „Configuration of Persistency“</a></p><h4>Entscheidung: Schlüssel oder Datei</h4><p>Wähle <code>KeyValueStorage</code> für adressierbare, typisierte Zustände mit einer expliziten Synchronisierungsgrenze; wähle <code>FileStorage</code> für dateiförmige Inhalte und Accessor-basiertes Lesen bzw. Schreiben. Initialwerte und initiale Dateien können mit Installation oder Update mitgeliefert werden. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.2">SWS Persistency §7.1.2 „Configuration of Key-Value Storages“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.3">SWS Persistency §7.1.3 „Configuration of File Storages“</a></p><p class="interp"><strong>Interpretation:</strong> Die Auswahl ist ein Datenmodell-Entscheid: kleine, logisch getrennte Zustände profitieren von Schlüsseln; zusammenhängende oder streamartige Inhalte passen eher zur Datei-Schnittstelle. Sie folgt aus den unterschiedlichen, in der Spezifikation beschriebenen Zugriffsmodellen.</p><h4>Betriebsmodell und Datenhaltbarkeit</h4><p>Ein geöffneter Key-Value Storage arbeitet zunächst auf temporären Daten. <code>SyncToStorage</code> schreibt alle Änderungen seit Öffnen oder letzter Synchronisierung dauerhaft und aktualisiert konfigurierte Redundanz; ohne Synchronisierung werden Änderungen beim Schließen oder Neustart verworfen. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=section.7.3">SWS Persistency §7.3 „Key-Value Storage specific Features“</a></p><p>Bei Dateien wird die konkrete Datei über einen Accessor geöffnet. Schreibzugriffe können über <code>SyncToFile</code> gezielt in den physischen Speicher übertragen werden; Ownership des Accessors ist exklusiv. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=section.7.4">SWS Persistency §7.4 „File Storage specific Features“</a></p><h4>Schutz, Wiederherstellung und Ressourcen</h4><p>Redundanz kann Integrität über Prüfsummen oder mehrere Kopien absichern; bei nicht behebbaren Befunden kann ein Recovery-Report-Callback die Anwendung informieren. Eine Wiederherstellung kann initiale oder ältere Daten ergeben und ist daher fachlich zu prüfen. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.2.4">SWS Persistency §7.2.4 „Redundancy Concepts“</a></p><p>Der konfigurierte Höchstwert begrenzt tatsächlich belegten Speicher. Die Größenabfragen enthalten Metadaten sowie Redundanz- und Backupbedarf und können bei offenem Storage oder parallelen Operationen ungenau sein. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.2.6">SWS Persistency §7.2.6 „Resource Management Concepts“</a></p><h4>Installation, Update und Rollback</h4><p>Die Target Configuration kann vordefinierte Werte und Dateien einbringen. Während der Verifikationsphase kann <code>UpdatePersistency</code> Änderungen nach neuen Konfigurationsdaten ausführen; nach erfolgreicher Finalisierung entfernt <code>CleanUpPersistency</code> Sicherungsdaten. Ist eine ältere Konfiguration aktiviert, erfolgt abhängig von der gespeicherten Backupversion eine Wiederherstellung oder Neuinstallation. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.2.5">SWS Persistency §7.2.5 „Installation and Update of Persistent Data“</a></p><div 4 Constraints and Assumptions
4.1 Known Limitations

Although a
Key-Value Storage
and
File Storage
can be configured as
write-only, the current API always allows read access. Read access is even pos-
sible when a
file
has been opened with
ara::per::FileStorage::Open-
FileWriteOnly
.
4.2 Constraints on Configuration
There are several constraints on the
Persistency
configuration that need to be ob-
served by the tooling which creates/processes this part of the
Execution Manifest
.
These constraints are defined in [3].
4.3 Assumptions about the Implementation of Persistency
Persistency
can be implemented with different internal architectures, and at the
same time,
applications
and other
functional clusters
expect a well defined
behavior that is independent of the actual implementation of
Persistency
. There-
fore, the specification in this document needs to be sufficiently generic to cover the
underlying differences. As usual in AUTOSAR Adaptive, the actual implementation is
not defined by the specification and is therefore entirely up to the vendor of
Persis-
tency
.
The following subsections list some of the possible implementations of
Persistency
.
4.3.1 Library Only
In this scenario,
Persistency
consists solely of a library. The manifest is partly used
to configure the compilation of the library (design time parts) and partly transferred to
a configuration file that is read by
Persistency
at run-time (deployment parts).
There is still some freedom regarding the storage of
metadata
and actual data, and
regarding the points in time when
elements
of a
storage
are checked regarding re-
dundancy or authenticity or when they are decrypted. E.g. the whole
File Storage
could be checked when it is opened or the single
files
could be checked when they
are opened.

4.3.2 Using a Central Daemon
In this scenario, the
Persistency
library connects in the background to a daemon
via some IPC mechanism. The manifest influences again the compilation of the library
part and is also transferred to configuration files for the library part and possibly also
the daemon.
An implementer has the same freedom regarding data storage, encryption, and checks
for redundancy and authenticity as in the last scenario. But an additional challenge is
that the communication channel between library and daemon can be lost at any time,
resulting in additional potential errors.
4.3.3 Based on a File System
Both a library and a daemon can access
storage
using the file system services of
the operating system. In this case, because AUTOSAR Adaptive is based on POSIX,
the file systems will be mounted with specific options that are out of control of the
Persistency
implementation, but influence the point in time when written data ac-
tually appears on the disc. Due to this, it is not possible to guarantee synchronous
behavior for calls like
ara::per::KeyValueStorage::SyncToStorage
or
ara::
per::ReadWriteAccessor::SyncToFile
.
4.3.4 Direct Access to Storage Hardware
Independently of whether a daemon is used or not,
Persistency
can be implemented
to access hardware devices like flash memory directly. These devices have the intrinsic
problem that the signal that can be read from each memory cell is reduced over time,
mainly influenced by the number of write accesses. In the end, the cell will produce
arbitrary values on each read access.
Unfortunately, the distribution of write accesses in typical systems is very uneven.
Some parameters might be updated a few times a second, while some code may stay
untouched for the whole life time of the ECU. To avoid early read errors, wear leveling
should be deployed, such that frequent updates of single data elements are distributed
over the whole memory area.
On the other hand, most operating systems include a file system or at least a flash
driver that takes care of wear leveling, such that a typical implementation of the
Per-
sistency
will not have to care about the wear leveling. This use case is therefore not
described in any detail in this specification.

The

stored in a

File Storage

applied and the used algorithms are decided at deployment time. The
application
is not aware of this fact.
If confidentiality of data shall be protected, a
storage
or an
element
of a
storage
are encrypted after the creation of the

and when the
storage
is saved, and

storage

storage

is saved, and verified

can be detected.

storage
(or an
element
therein) by calculating a hash value of the data to be pro-
tected and comparing this calculated value to a hash value provided in the
manifest
.

mechanisms (like secure boot).

(like AES GCM) can be used.

8 API Specification
The APIs for accessing
File Storages
and
Key-Value Storage
are completely
separate, and therefore divided into separate sections. Additional sections describe
common functionality.
The API of
Persistency
is designed around the
ara::per::SharedHandle
and
ara::per::UniqueHandle
, which are returned by factory functions like
ara::
per::OpenKeyValueStorage
or
ara::per::FileStorage::OpenFileRead-
Write
. The classes defined in this chapter cannot be constructed directly by the
Adaptive Application
, and consequently the default constructors are considered
to be not publicly accessible (i.e. to be deleted, private, or protected).
8.1 General Features of Persistency
8.1.1 ara::core Types
The
ara::per
API is based heavily on the
ara::core
types defined in [2].
ara::core::Result
is used wherever possible, and because of this, most methods
are defined as
noexcept
.
Consequently, in situations where memory cannot be allocated for new objects, the
Persistency
shall terminate the process by calling
ara::core::Abort
(see [2]).

8.1.3 Redundancy Handling
The
Persistency
supports redundant storage of
Key-Value Storages
,
File
Storages
, and the
key-value pairs
and
files
contained in these. An error in
the stored data that can be fixed using the redundantly stored data will be implicitly
fixed when the
Key-Value Storage
or
File Storage
is accessed, an error is only
returned by
Persistency
when the redundancy fails. To be able to track whether
storage
errors have been fixed using the available redundancy, the
application
can register the following callback function.

Opens a Key-Value Storage.
OpenKeyValueStorage will fail with kResourceBusy when the Key-Value Storage is currently
being modified by a call from another thread to UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, Reset
Persistency, RecoverKeyValueStorage, or ResetKeyValueStorage.
Because multiple threads can access the same Key-Value Storage concurrently, the Key-Value
Storage might not be closed when the SharedHandle returned by this function goes out of
scope. It will only be closed when all SharedHandles that refer to the same Key-Value Storage
went out of scope.

OpenFileStorage will fail with kResourceBusy when the File Storage is currently being modified
by a call from another thread to UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, ResetPersistency,
RecoverAllFiles, or ResetAllFiles.
Because multiple threads can access the same File Storage concurrently, the File Storage might
not be closed when the SharedHandle returned by this function goes out of scope. It will only be
closed when all SharedHandles that refer to the same File Storage went out of scope.

Writes the content of a StringView to the file.
The time when the content is persisted depends on the implementation of Persistency. SyncTo
File can be used to force Persistency to persist the file content.
In case of an error, the file content might be corrupted, and the current position might or might
not have changed.
The expected state of the file for each supported error can be expected to be as follows:

kPhysicalStorageFailure: The state of the file is unknown. It could have been entirely
destroyed.

kEncryptionFailed: The content of the file and the current position will have been updated, but
could not be persisted. The persisted file will reflect an older version of the file.

kOutOfStorageSpace: The content of the file will have been updated, but the part of the
operation that exceeded the quota will have been discarded. The current position will be at
the end of the file.
